For those who fear Allah, there are with their Lord gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they shall live forever, and wives purified, and approval from Allah. They will also have wives who will be free from any defects in their form or character. After talking about the enemies, describing their life, and explaining their furthest goal, God in this verse comes back to the story of the friends. Here someone hopes for the Garden of the Refuge and is told, "Flee from the unlawful and be just, and that will not be held back from you. According to a hadith in Jami al-Tirmidhi, the Holy Prophet said: 'If a dweller of Paradise wishes to have children, the process of pregnancy, birth and growth of the child will be completed in no time and he would have what he wished for.'. So, among the blessings of the Akhirah, the mention of 'wives purified' was considered sufficient because the Holy Qur'an has another promise for the people of Paradise: 57 And for them there is what they wish for).

**What the money of this world leads to, and the life to come.**

(Allah is Seer of His bondmen) He is Seer of the believers, their places in Paradise, as well as their works in the life of this world. He is so engrossed in building the future of his children in this world, that he no longer remembers the fact that there is any ‘future’ beyond this present life, to which he should give thought. Making money, accumulating riches and possessing property in this world seem so estimable to him, that he fails to realize that there is any ‘wealth’ other than this, to which he should devote his life. Sometimes, the want for more money is for the purpose of spending it on acts of worship, being kind to the family, the relatives, and spending on various acts of righteousness and obedience; this behavior is praised and encouraged in the religion. God, wishing to ascertain which of His creatures are capable of rising above worldly attractions, has so willed it that man should be attracted to and find gratification in the things of this world, but at the same time be faced with the choice of clinging to them or renouncing them in favour of the unseen things of the next world. Out of the rest, children were not mentioned because man loves children during his life in the world as children help and strengthen him in what he does and through them his name lives on. Providing all comforts for his home in this world becomes so dear to him that it never occurs to him that there is any other home save this, to which he should pay heed.

**What Allah keeps for those who fear Him, and the place of the horses.**

In the other world, there is no travel and no riding but, sound hadith reports do prove that fine horses will be presented before the dwellers of Paradise on Fridays which they will ride to go and meet friends and relatives. The Splendorous Qur'an ties the two together in its words, "As for him who fears the standing place be fore his Lord and prohibits the soul its caprice, surely the Garden shall be the shelter" [79:40-41]. (Every Arabian horse is allowed to have two supplications every dawn, and the horse supplicates, 'O Allah! You made me subservient to the son of Adam. Therefore, make me among the dearest of his wealth and household to him, or, ...make me the dearest of his household and wealth to him.) Allah sees the actions of His servants, nothing is hidden from Him and He will recompense them for what they do. Then Allah elucidated the bliss of the Hereafter, its permanence and favour, just as He exposited the joys of the life of this world, by saying: This is not an easy choice, for he sees that worldly acquisitions lead him to an honourable place in society. By possessing material resources, he can have all that he wants in life. Similarly, gold and silver were not mentioned in relation to the Paradise because gold and silver are needed in the mortal world as material things are bought against them or anything else one-needs can be procured through them. This is why in this case, these horses provide a shield of sufficiency for their owner, as evident by a Hadith that we will mention, Allah willing, when we explain Allah's statement,. According to a hadith, when the people of Paradise would have settled down there, happy and content without having any desire remaining unfulfilled, Allah Almighty will speak to them asking if they are happy and if they need anything. It will be recalled that in the preceding verse , the total count of blessings that infatuate man was given as six women, children, heaps of gold and silver, fine horses, cattle and tillage.

16.text:
The verse gives the words of the people whose description has just been completed, so the praise that surrounds them ends in a prayer rather than in a claim. "who pray, Our Lord" identifies them by what they do and not by what they are, and the address opens with the Lord and not with themselves, which the sources take as the shape of a request that expects an answer. "We have believed" states the ground of the request first, and the past tense gives the faith as something already settled, so the asking rests on what has already been given. "so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire" then asks twice, first for the removal of what is past and then for safety in what is to come, and the order is kept because forgiveness comes before protection in the wording as it does in the need. The asking is joined to the belief by the letter of consequence, so the two are one movement, and the torment is named without being described, since the verse tells what they ask for and not what they fear.

**The prayer of the believers, and the Lord they address.**

Those alladhīna is either an adjectival qualification of or a substitution for the previous alladhīna who say “O Our Lord we believe in You and in Your Prophet; so forgive us our sins and guard us from the chastisement of the Fire”. (Those who say: "Our Lord! We have indeed believed") in You, Your Book and Your Messenger. (Lo! we believe) in You and in Your Messenger. The people of Paradise are the ones who say in their prayers, ‘Our Lord, we have faith in You and in that which You revealed to Your messengers; and we have followed Your sacred law. O Our Lord we believe; so forgive us our sins and guard us from the chastisement of the fire that is they occupy themselves with Us entirely bi-l-kulliya and plead for help before Us at the mention of severe trials and afflictions al-raziyya. Allah then proceeds to describe them, saying:

**The forgiveness of sins, the gardens, and the wives made pure.**

(So forgive us our sins) that we committed in the pre-Islamic period as well as after the advent of Islam (and guard us from the punishment of Fire) drive away from us the punishment of hell;. As compared to that, only three blessings of the Hereafter, that is, the gardens of Par-adise, wives purified and the approval from Allah have been identified. For those who fear Allah, there are with their Lord gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they shall live forever, and wives purified, and approval from Allah. According to a hadith in Jami al-Tirmidhi, the Holy Prophet said: 'If a dweller of Paradise wishes to have children, the process of pregnancy, birth and growth of the child will be completed in no time and he would have what he wished for.'.

**The conviction that the next world is in the hands of the Lord.**

He will be filled with the conviction that the matters of the next world are entirely in the hands of his Lord and all the glitter of this world will appear meaningless. As a result, God will be the entity he fears most and he will be desirous of the next life more than anything else. He will not follow his mundane desires, but will rather determine his course of action, keeping in view the court of the Almighty. Whatever difficulties he faces in the path of his Creator, he will adhere to that path with total steadfastness, because he will have the conviction that no one can give him succour if he turns away from God.

**What the asking in the last hours of the night shows.**

(those who spend) from their wealth on all the acts of obedience they were commanded, being kind to kith and kin, helping the needy, and comforting the destitute. (Every night, when the last third of it remains, our Lord, the Blessed, the Superior, descends to the lowest heaven saying, "Is there anyone to ask Me, so that I may grant him his request? Is there anyone to invoke Me, so that I may respond to his invocation? Is there anyone seeking My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?") (and those who pray and beg Allah's pardon in the last hours of the night) and this testifies to the virtue of seeking Allah's forgiveness in the latter part of the night. Those obtain nearness and intimate friendship al-qurba wa-l-khuṣūṣiyya with Us high degrees wa-l-darajāt al-ʿuliyya and pleasing fates wa-l qisam al-murḌiyya.

17.text:
The verse describes the same people with four words and then with one practice, and the practice is the one the sources single out because of its hour. "It is they who are patient, sincere, obedient, and charitable" gathers the marks of the guided into a single sentence, and the order runs from what a person keeps back, to what he means by his word, to what he gives out, and the sources read patience here as patience in obedience and against disobedience, and not only patience under harm. "and who pray for forgiveness before dawn" ends the description with an act done at an hour when no one is watching and the self is asleep, so the asking is placed where praise is not the motive, and the last part of the night is given the place of honour in the wording. The four words and the prayer together answer the plea of the verses before them, and they show the marks by which the gardens named earlier are sought, and the verse that follows turns from the people to a warning, so the description stands as the shape of the life the sūrah is calling to.

**The patient, the truthful, the obedient, and the charitable.**

The patient in obedience and against disobedience al-sābirīna ‘the patient’ is an adjectival qualification of alladhīna ‘those’ truthful in their faith obedient compliant before God expenders of charity imploring God’s pardon by saying ‘Lord forgive us’ at daybreak’ in the last part of the night singled out here for mention because it is the time of unawareness and of the joy of sleep. (They are) the patient, the true believers, and obedient with sincere devotion in worship to Allah. They are the ones who are patient in doing good actions, leaving bad actions and in the face of calamity; truthful in their words and actions; fulfil Allah’s sacred law completely; spend their wealth in Allah’s path; and ask for forgiveness in the last part of the night when prayers are most likely accepted and when hearts are not distracted. ((They are) those who are patient) while performing acts of obedience and abandoning the prohibitions.

**Patience in obedience and against disobedience.**

(The steadfast) in performing the obligations enjoined by Allah and in shunning contraventions against Him; it is also said that this means: the steadfast when misfortunes befall them, (and the Truthful) in their faith, (and the obedient) vis-�-vis Allah and His Messenger, (those who spend) their wealth in the way of Allah, (those who pray for pardon in the watches of the night) supererogatory prayers. The patient, that is, with their hearts, the truthful with their spirits, the devoted with their souls, the expenders of what they are able, those who ask forgiveness with their tongues.2 The chevaliers are those whose speaking is this and whose doing is this. In the heart they are patient with the Real's command, in the spirit they walk straight in the Real's covenant, in the body they observe the right ful due of the Real's command, with wealth they spend in the Real's road, with tongue they ask forgiveness and seek from the Real's generosity.

**The asking for forgiveness before dawn.**

The hour is part of the meaning, and the sources treat it as the proof of sincerity. (and those who pray and beg Allah's pardon in the last hours of the night) and this testifies to the virtue of seeking Allah's forgiveness in the latter part of the night. (Every night, when the last third of it remains, our Lord, the Blessed, the Superior, descends to the lowest heaven saying, "Is there anyone to ask Me, so that I may grant him his request? Is there anyone to invoke Me, so that I may respond to his invocation? Is there anyone seeking My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?") Those who spend [in good] and those who pray and beg Allah's pardon in the last hours of the night.

**The conviction, and the desire for the next world.**

He will not follow his mundane desires, but will rather determine his course of action, keeping in view the court of the Almighty. As a result, God will be the entity he fears most and he will be desirous of the next life more than anything else. He will be filled with the conviction that the matters of the next world are entirely in the hands of his Lord and all the glitter of this world will appear meaningless. Whatever difficulties he faces in the path of his Creator, he will adhere to that path with total steadfastness, because he will have the conviction that no one can give him succour if he turns away from God.

**What will be given to the patient at dawn.**

The patient, the truthful, the devoted, the expenders, those who ask forgiveness at dawn. " Some day good fortune will enter my door, some day the sun of elation will rise, Some day You will cast a glance at me, some day this sorrow of mine will end. According to a hadith in Jami al-Tirmidhi, the Holy Prophet said: 'If a dweller of Paradise wishes to have children, the process of pregnancy, birth and growth of the child will be completed in no time and he would have what he wished for.'.

18.text:
The verse stands at the head of the passage as the testimony on which everything after it rests, and it gives the witness first, then those who bear it with Him. "Allah Himself is a Witness that there is no god worthy of worship except Him" opens with the witness of the Lord to His own oneness, and the wording makes the statement the object of the testimony, so the fact is given as something made clear rather than as something argued. "and so are the angels and people of knowledge" then joins the angels and the learned to the same testimony, and the order is kept because the angels are named for their nearness and the people of knowledge for what they carry from the messengers, so the verse honours knowledge by placing it in that company. "He is the Maintainer of justice" describes the witness as the one who keeps the whole creation in order, and the word is understood of both the showing of what is true and the holding of the world in measure, so the testimony and the ordering are one act. "There is no god worthy of worship except Him, the Almighty, All-Wise" repeats the statement and names two of His names in it, and the repetition is not idle, since the first statement carries the gift of oneness and the second carries the power that none can resist and the wisdom that orders what it wills. The verse comes after a passage about those who were given knowledge and kept it from its people, and it sets the testimony of God, the angels and the learned against their turning away.

**The witness of God to His own oneness.**

God bears witness that is to say He has made it clear to His creation through proofs and signs that there is no god none that is truly worshipped in existence except Him He has borne witness to this and the angels have also borne witness to this by affirming it and those of knowledge from among the prophets and the believers through their conviction and in words; upholding constantly and uniquely maintaining His creations with justice qā’iman ‘upholding’ is in the accusative because it is a circumstantial qualifier and is governed by the import of the statement implied to be something like tafarrada ‘He alone is upholding…’; there is no god except Him He has repeated it for emphasis; the Mighty in His Kingdom the Wise in His actions. Allah bears witness that none has the right to be worshipped but He, and the angels, and those having knowledge (also bear witness to this); (He always) maintains His creation in justice. Allah testifies that He alone is worthy of worship based on the legislative and universal signs indicating His divinity. The Real bears witness to the Real that He is the Real.

**The angels and the people of knowledge as witnesses.**

The two are joined in one sentence, and the sources weigh what each one's testimony carries. The second testimony mentioned is that of angels who are close to Allah. It means that the being and the attributes of Allah and the manifestations of His power and creativity all over are open signs of His Oneness. The angels and people of knowledge also testify to this, by declaring and calling to His Oneness. None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Almighty, the All-Wise Truly, the religion with Allah is Islam. (Allah (Himself) is witness) even if no one else bears witness (that there is no God save Him. And the angels) do also bear witness to that (and the men of learning) and the prophets and the believers bear witness to that.

**The Maintainer of justice, and what the word carries.**

(Maintaining His creation in justice, there is no God save Him, the Almighty) in His vengeance against those who do not believe in Him, (the Wise) and He has commanded that none shall be worshipped except Him. The God of the universe is the One and only God and He likes justice. Each and every part of the universe is in a complete state of ‘surrender’, that is, all its functions are performed in accordance with the appointed plan of God. They testified to the greatest thing anyone can testify to; the absolute right of Allah to be worshipped, and the perfect justice in His creation and sacred law.

**The Most Truthful and Just Witness, the Mighty and the Wise.**

There is no god but Him, the Mighty who can never be overpowered and the one who is Wise in His creation, planning and legislation. Making anyone else, save God, the centre of his attention or nurturing the thought that God’s judgement can be based on anything other than justice is inconceivable in the present universe. Allah bears witness, and verily, Allah is sufficient as a Witness, and He is the Most Truthful and Just Witness there is; His statement is the absolute truth,. None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Almighty, the All-Wise Truly, the religion with Allah is Islam.

**What the verse does in the passage, and the knowledge it honours.**

It is also possible that the term, ulul ilm (the men of knowledge) may, in an absolute sense, be referring to those who, by conducting an inquiry based on sound intellectual principles, or by deliberating into this universe, could acquire the knowl-edge of the unity of Allah Almighty - even if they are not alim or 'men of knowledge' in the traditional sense, whose knowledge is acquired under a formal discipline from Islam's own original sources. The vast universe run by its Master through His unseen agents, the angels, is exactly what it ought to be and as perfect as it can be. According to established knowledge, the universe seems to be a completely unitary system. He Himself praised Himself and He Him self gave witness to Himself concerning His attributes as is worthy of Himself. Then there are the Messengers and Books sent by Allah, all confirming. that truth. (And say to those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and to those who are illiterates (Arab pagans): "Do you (also) submit yourselves?" If they do, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the Message.) meaning, their reckoning is with Allah and their return and final destination is to Him. Allah then states that those who were given the Scripture beforehand divided in the religion after Allah sent the Messengers and revealed the Books to them providing them the necessary proofs to not do so.

**The love of the witness, and the words kept with it.**

Whoever recites this verse and then says: ; (And to that, 0 my Lord, I too am a witness), Allah Almighty will say to the angels on the Last Day: 'My servant has made a promise while I am the Foremost to keep a promise when I make it, so let my servant be admitted into Paradise.' (Ibn Kathir) (By He in Whose Hand is my soul! No member of this Ummah, no Jew or Christian, hears of me but dies without believing in what I was sent with, but will be among the people of the Fire.) Muslim recorded this Hadith. There was no universe and no Adam, no air and no space, no land and no sea, no light and no darkness, no understanding and no virtue, no conformity and no hypocrisy when the Lord of the Worlds spoke in the majesty of His measure and the perfection of His exaltedness, giving witness to His oneness and peerlessness and reporting of His attributes and Essence. He bore witness to the majesty of His measure and the perfection of His exaltedness while there was no refusal, no ignorance, no recognition by any created thing, no intellect, no conformity, no hy pocrisy, no new arrival, no heaven, no space, no shadows, no brightness.

19.text:
The verse names the religion that God accepts and then shows why those who dispute about it are not disputing over evidence. "Certainly, Allah, s only Way is Islam" states the matter as settled, and the word carries both the general sense of submitting to God and the particular sense of the community that answers the final messenger, and the sources keep both because the sentence keeps them together. "Those who were given the Scripture did not dispute among themselves out of mutual envy until knowledge came to them" then turns to the people who had the earlier books, and the wording places the disagreement after the knowledge and names the motive as envy, so the dispute is described as a matter of the self and not of the evidence, and the sources notice that the knowledge is what should have removed the difference rather than deepened it. "Whoever denies Allah, s signs" states the condition on the other side, and the signs include what the messengers brought and what the world itself shows. "then surely Allah is swift in reckoning" closes with the requital, and the swiftness is set against the delay they counted on, since the account may come in this life or in the next and nothing is missed. The passage before this one described the testimony of God and the learned, and this verse shows the community that carries it, while the verse after it turns from the claim to the argument itself. The verse is placed between the testimony of the learned and the argument that follows, and it names both what God accepts and the reason a people who had the books still divided over it. The claim is not that the books differed but that the people did, and the difference came after the proof had reached them, so the passage keeps the gift and the warning in one place.

**The religion that is accepted with God.**

Lo! the religion with God pleasing to Him is submission to the One God al-islām that is to say the Divine Law with which the messengers were sent founded upon the affirmation of God’s Oneness a variant reading for inna ‘lo!’ has anna ‘that’ as an inclusive substitution for annahu to the end of that verse sc. shahida Llāhu … anna l-dīna ‘inda Llāhi l-islām ‘God bears witness that religion with God is Islām. Now the real meaning of the word, Islam is to submit oneself to Allah and be obedient to His commands. (Lo! Religion) that is accepted (with Allah the Surrender (to His will and guidance). The acceptable path in Allah’s sight is Islam, the path of surrendering: devotion of all good actions to Allah alone, submission to Him in servitude and acceptance of all messengers, including the final messenger Muhammad ﷺ with whom revelations came to an end, and after whom no sacred laws will remain valid except his. Surely the religion with God is the submission.

**The submission named among the prophets and their communities.**

The sense of surrender is one, and the community that carries it is named by the same word. Given this meaning, those who believed in the prophets and messengers of their time and were obedient to the commands of Allah they brought to them, were all entitled to be called Muslims, and their religion was Islam. Similarly, the Islam of the period of Sayyidna Musa was what came in the form of the tablets of Torah and the teachings of Moses and the Islam of the period of Sayyidna Isa was what came as Injil and the teachings of Jesus At the end of this chain of prophets, the Islam of the period of Sayyidna Muhammad the last among the prophets shall be what took shape on the pattern given by the Qur'an and Sunnah. It was in this sense of the word that Sayyidna Nuh said: ‌ I have been commanded that I be from among the Muslims 10:72) and therefore, Sayyidna Ibrahim described himself and his community as Muslims when he said: ‌ ‌ (Our Lord, make us Muslims, the submitting ones to Thee, and from our progeny a community of Muslims submitting to Thee - 2:128). If the first meaning is taken, it would mean that the only religion -acceptable with Allah is Islam, that is, becoming obedient in complete submission to the commands of Allah, believing in all prophets of all times and in whatever commandments they brought, by acting accordingly.

**The one religion of the prophets.**

This tells us that the din of all our blessed prophets was one and the same, that is, belief in the most perfect Being and Attributes of Allah, in His being free of all shortcomings and- that He alone is worthy of worship, believing in this from the depth of one's heart and confirming it verbally; belief in the Day of Judgment, in the final reckoning of deeds, the reward and the punishment and in Paradise and Hell and in every prophet and messenger sent by Him and in all command-ments and injunctions brought by them, believing all this in one's heart and confirming such belief verbally as well. Therefore, whatever meaning of Islam is taken, general or particular, in relation to the community being addressed by the Holy Qur'an, the outcome of both is nothing but that, following the appearance of the noble Prophet the only religion which shall be deserving of the Surah 'Al- Imran 3.18-19 name, Islam, will be the one that conforms to the and the teachings of the blessed recipient of revelations and that alone shall be acceptable in the sight of Allah. This assertion is made in all the revealed scriptures which are still in their original form.

**The people of the Book, and the dispute after knowledge.**

Those who were given the Scripture the Jews and the Christians differed in religion some affirming God’s Oneness others rejecting it only after the knowledge of Oneness came to them through transgression on the part of the disbelievers among themselves. Those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) did not differ except out of rivalry, after knowledge had come to them. (Those who (formerly) received the Scripture) the Jews and Christians (differed) about Islam and Muhammad (only after knowledge) the exposition of what is in their Scripture (came unto them, through transgression among themselves) out of resentful envy. The Jews and Christians only split up into various groups and sects, after evidence was established against them in the form of knowledge that had come to them, because of envy and greed for the world.

**The denial of the signs, and the Jews and Christians who deny them.**

Yet for whoever denies the verses of Allah revealed to His Messenger, Allah is quick in taking to account those who disbelieve in Him and His messengers. (And say to those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and to those who are illiterates (Arab pagans): "Do you (also) submit yourselves?" If they do, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the Message.) meaning, their reckoning is with Allah and their return and final destination is to Him. (By He in Whose Hand is my soul! No member of this Ummah, no Jew or Christian, hears of me but dies without believing in what I was sent with, but will be among the people of the Fire.) Muslim recorded this Hadith.

**What the witness of God and the learned shows, and what follows it.**

Allah bears witness that Religion with Him is Islam (the Surrender), and the angels, the prophets and the believers also bear witness to this. Making anyone else, save God, the centre of his attention or nurturing the thought that God’s judgement can be based on anything other than justice is inconceivable in the present universe. The God of the universe is the One and only God and He likes justice. This verse was revealed about two men from Historic Syria who asked the Prophet ﷺ which is the greatest witness in the Book of Allah. The first way station is the acknowledgment that spares blood and wealth: the person's neck is safe from the sword and his wealth is left with him, whether he is a conformer or a hypocrite, a follower or an innovator. It is to throw oneself on the Real's exalted thresh old and follow Him, approving of His decree, not protesting against it or turning away from it, and having reverence and respect for it. These verses have very clearly hit at the root of the atheistic approach which endeavours to bracket Islam and disbelief (kufr) on the same footing in the name of tolerance preached by Islam, thereby claiming that every faith of the world Judaism, Christianity, even paganism can each become the source of salvation, on condition that its followers perform good deeds and observe good morals.

20.text:
The verse answers the argument with a statement rather than with a counter-argument, and it puts the answer in the mouth of the Prophet before it turns to the others. "So if they argue with you O Prophet, say" lets the argument happen and then moves past it, and the sources read the command as a direction away from disputing over what is already clear. "I have submitted myself to Allah" gives the reply in the first person and in the form of a surrender, so the Prophet answers with what he is and not with what he can prove, and "and so have my followers" widens the same statement to the community that stands with him. "And ask those who were given the Scripture and the illiterate people" then sends the same question to both bodies, the people of the earlier books and the people who had no book, and the pairing shows that the demand is one and the same for both. "Have you submitted yourselves to Allah" is the question, and it is the same word as the statement before it, so the two sides are measured by one standard. "If they submit" states the condition, and "they will be rightly guided" gives the outcome, since guidance is tied to the surrender and to nothing else. "But if they turn away" sets the other case, and "then your duty is only to deliver the message" frees the Prophet from the answer they give, since the work given him is the delivery and not the result. "And Allah is All-Seeing of His servants" ends by naming the one who sees what every servant does with the message, and the passage before this one described the knowledge that was kept back, so the argument here is shown as the last stage of a long refusal.

**The argument, and the answer given to the Prophet.**

So if they the disbelievers dispute with you O Muhammad concerning religion say to them ‘I have surrendered my countenance to God that is to say I have submitted to Him I and whoever follows me’ wajh ‘countenance’ is chosen here because of its noble character for the other parts of the body will just as soon surrender once the countenance has; and say to those who have been given the Scripture the Jews and the Christians and to the uninstructed the Arab idolaters ‘Have you submitted?’ that is to say ‘Submit! (And if they) i.e. the Jews and Christians (argue with thee, O Muhammad, say: I have surrendered my purpose) I make my Religion and works sincere (to Allah and (so have) those who follow me. And say unto those who have received the Scripture) the Jews and Christians (and those who read not) i.e. the Arabs: (And say to those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) and to those who are illiterates (Arab pagans): "Do you (also) submit yourselves?" If they do, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the Message.) meaning, their reckoning is with Allah and their return and final destination is to Him. If they argue with you, O Messenger, about the truth that has been revealed to you, then say to them in reply, ‘I and the believers who follow me have submitted to Allah’. Answered here are argumentations in which the disbelievers and deniers among the people of the Book persist - even after the truth of Islam has been proved conclusively. The Surah began with the confirmation of Divine Oneness and the refutation of Trinity. Also, say, O Messenger, to the People of the Scripture and the idolaters, ‘Do you submit to Allah sincerely, following what I have brought? Allah commanded His servant and Messenger, Muhammad , to call the People of the Two Scriptures and the unlettered idolators to his religion, way, Law and all that Allah sent him with.

**The surrender of the self, and those who follow.**

The first person keeps the answer personal, and the second clause widens it to the community. I have surrendered my countenance to God and whoever follows me : and say to those who have been given the scripture and to the uninstructed: The Holy Prophet was entrusted with the mission of calling the people of the Book, the Jews and Christians, and the disbelievers of Arabia to submit to Allah and embrace Islam which will be for their own good for they will be on the right path. The advice against such ongoing. and unnecessary disputations is that the acceptance or rejection of disputers should be of no use to a believer who simply has to declare that he and those with him have entered the fold of Islam being in no doubt about its truth. (Say: "I have submitted myself to Allah (in Islam), and (so have) those who follow me") meaning, Say, 'I have made my worship sincere for Allah Alone without partners, rivals, offspring or companion,.

**Those who are guided, and those who turn away.**

’ And so if they have submitted they have been guided from error but if they turn their backs to Islam your duty is only to deliver the Message; and God sees His servants and so requites them for their deeds — this statement was revealed before the command to fight them had been revealed. (If they surrender) as you have surrendered, (then truly they are rightly guided) from error, (and if they turn away) from surrender, (then it is your duty only to convey the message (unto them) on behalf of Allah.

**The duty of delivery, and the sight of God.**

In case they continue to maintain their hostile attitude, the Holy Prophet has been comforted here by saying that his duty is only limited to conveying the message of Allah and His commandments. Occupy your tongue by counseling them but empty your heart of their talk and separate your innermost self from witnessing them for We have not charged you with their affairs [but only] with deliver[ing] [the message]. (By He in Whose Hand is my soul! No member of this Ummah, no Jew or Christian, hears of me but dies without believing in what I was sent with, but will be among the people of the Fire.) Muslim recorded this Hadith. All their plans to censor the dayees’ words will fail, and when God’s scales of justice are put in place, they will see that those actions, which had given them the conviction of securing success and salvation, are quite without value. One who looks at created beings through the eye of [God's] delib erative power qudra knows that the One who determines for all based on what He has chosen for each is One. The Two Sahihs and other collections of Hadith recorded that the Prophet sent letters to the kings of the earth during his time and to different peoples, Arabs and non-Arabs, People of the Book and the unlettered, just as Allah had commanded him. 'Abdur-Razzaq recorded that Ma'mar said, that Hammam said that Abu Hurayrah said that the Prophet said,.

**Islam, the prophets, and the sense of superiority.**

The call of the Quran is the call of the same true version of Islam, the religion of submission to God, as was revealed to all the other prophets. Those who deny this do so, not because its truth is not clear to them, but because of their own sense of superiority. Acknowledging its veracity amounts, as they see it, to accepting the intellectual superiority of the proponent of the Quran. Instead of accepting the truth, they want to exterminate the dayee himself. Those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians) did not differ except out of rivalry, after knowledge had come to them. Allah then mentions their argument with the Prophet ﷺ about the Religion of Islam, saying: Allah then states that those who were given the Scripture beforehand divided in the religion after Allah sent the Messengers and revealed the Books to them providing them the necessary proofs to not do so. This and similar Ayat are clear proofs that the Message of Muhammad is universal to all creation, as it is well established in the religion, according to the various texts of the Book and Sunnah. That the message does not seem to get across to them, as they elect to reject rather than accept, should really not be a matter of concern for him.

21.text:
The verse names three deeds in one breath and then answers them with the opposite of what they expect, and the three are set out so that the last is the worst. "Indeed, those who deny Allah, s signs" opens with the denial of what is plain, and the sources read the people meant as those who had the book and then denied what came to them, so the denial is joined to knowledge rather than to ignorance. "kill the prophets unjustly" names the killing of the messengers sent to them, and the word unjustly removes every cause they might claim, so the deed is left without any ground at all. "and kill people who stand up for justice" then names those who were put to death for speaking what is right, and the sources describe them as men who urged the good and were killed for it, so the verse covers the messengers and those who carried their word. "give them good news of a painful punishment" answers the whole list with a sentence that sounds like a promise and means the opposite, and the sources dwell on the choice of words, since good news is for what a person welcomes and here it is given to those who are about to meet what they ran from. The verse before described the community that carries the message, and this one shows what was done to those who carried it before.

**The denial of the signs by the people of the Book.**

In verse 21, 'those who disbelieve the verses of Allah' refers to Jews who did not believe in the Injil and the Qur'an. 'Slay the Prophets unjustly means that they know that they are doing so without justice. 'Those who bid justice' are people who teach moderation in deeds and morals. Verily, those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah and kill the Prophets without right, and kill those men who order just dealings, then announce to them a painful torment They are those whose works will be lost in this world and in the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers. (Lo! those who disbelieve the revelations of Allah) in Muhammad and the Qur'an, (and slay the Prophets) i.e. ally themselves with those who slay the prophets (wrongfully) without them having committed any crime, (and slay those of mankind) who believed in the prophets (who enjoin equity) Allah's divine Oneness: Those who disbelieve in Allah’s signs, which show that He alone is the Lord and the One worthy of being worshipped, kill His prophets wrongly due to hatred, and kill those who call for justice by commanding good and forbidding evil – give these murderous disbelievers news of a painful punishment.

Those who disbelieve in the signs of God and slay yaqtulūna is also read as yuqātilūna ‘they fight against’ the prophets without right and slay those who enjoin to equity to justice and these are the Jews who are reported to have killed forty–three prophets and to have been forbidden this by a hundred and seventy devout worshippers among them each of whom was killed immediately. Those who disbelieve in the signs of God and slay the prophets without right and slay those who enjoin to equity.

**The tidings given to them, and the painful punishment.**

The word is a rebuke, and the sources read the sentence as a whole. The use of ‘good tidings’ here is meant as a sarcastic ridicule of them the fā’ of fa-bashshirhum so give them good tidings is considered part of the predicate of inna because its noun that is its relative clause resembles a conditional sc. in yakfurūna ‘if they disbelieve…’ fa-bashshirhum ‘then give them good tidings…’. (then announce to them a painful torment) meaning, painful and humiliating,. (promise them a painful doom) which will spread out to their hearts.

Because of this whole set of their terrible deeds, verse 22 says that all their good deeds have gone waste both here and there, and when they are punished, they will find no one to assist them. Those whom We have bound to disappointment khidhlān and branded with the state of deprivation ḥirmān-tell them that Our turning away from them is perpetual and that We have already determined their transference from one abode of disgrace hawān to another from disap pointment khidhlān and deprivation ḥirmān to punishment and fires nīrān.

22.text:
The verse states what becomes of the deeds just described, and it is short because the verdict needs no elaboration. "They are the ones whose deeds are wasted in this world and the Hereafter" names the loss in both abodes at once, and the sources notice that the two are joined because the work done for a good end is spoiled in the same motion in which the doer refuses the truth. "And they will have no helpers" closes the verdict, and the word covers every kind of support, so no one stands for them when the account is taken, and the sources place this after the killing of the prophets to show that the loss is the outcome of the deeds and not an arbitrary sentence. The verse before described the murder of the messengers and of those who called for justice, and this one shows where such a road ends.

**The works that fail in this world and the Hereafter.**

Those are the ones whose works what good they did in the way of charity and kindness to kin have failed whose works are invalid in this world and the Hereafter and so they have nothing to reckon with since these works are of no consequence; they have no helpers no protectors from the chastisement. (Those are they whose works) good deeds (have failed) made void (in the world and the Hereafter) that is, they will not be given reward for them in the Hereafter; (and they have no helpers) who will save them from Allah's punishment. **The works they lose, and the help that will not come.**

The helpers are the last thing a person counts on, and the verse removes them. Because of this whole set of their terrible deeds, verse 22 says that all their good deeds have gone waste both here and there, and when they are punished, they will find no one to assist them. Such dissenters will enter the next world divested of all support. Those are the ones for whom no success is granted in their works tawfīq bi-aʿmāl today nor realization of their hopes taḥqīq li-āmāl tomorrow. That is only because they have lost Our help in both abodes and did not bear witness to Our might and power.
