They also killed many Prophets when they conveyed to them what Allah legislated for them, without cause or criminal behavior committed by these Prophets, for they only called them to the truth,. Ruh al-Ma'ani while commenting on this verse reports a hadith from the Holy Prophet as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim . All their plans to censor the dayees’ words will fail, and when God’s scales of justice are put in place, they will see that those actions, which had given them the conviction of securing success and salvation, are quite without value. In verse 21, 'those who disbelieve the verses of Allah' refers to Jews who did not believe in the Injil and the Qur'an. 'Slay the Prophets unjustly means that they know that they are doing so without justice. 'Those who bid justice' are people who teach moderation in deeds and morals. Verily, those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah and kill the Prophets without right, and kill those men who order just dealings, then announce to them a painful torment They are those whose works will be lost in this world and in the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers. This is why when they rejected the truth and acted arrogantly towards the creation, Allah punished them with humiliation and disgrace in this life, and humiliating torment in the Hereafter.

23.text:
The verse asks the Prophet to look at a case in front of him, and the whole of it turns on what people do when they are called to the book they claim. "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures" names the people meant, and the word for portion is stopped at by the sources, since it marks what they took from the book and what they left, and the ones meant had the Torah in their hands and still did not carry it out. "Yet when they are invited to the Book of Allah to settle their disputes" describes the invitation itself, and the invitation is to the book they already hold, so the matter does not turn on a new revelation but on what is written in what they have. "some of them turn away heedlessly" narrows the answer to a party among them rather than to all, and the word for turning away carries the sense of going aside with the face, so the refusal is shown as a movement of the body and not only as a decision of the mind. The sources set the verse in a known case, where a dispute was brought to the Prophet and the verdict in the Torah was the same as his, and the refusal came after the book had given its answer. The passage before this one described the people whose deeds fail in both abodes, and the verse that follows takes up the claim they made about the fire, so the turning away here is shown to be the habit of a people and not the slip of a moment.

**Those who were given a portion of the Book.**

Have you not seen those who were given a portion a share of the Book the Torah being called to the Book of God yud‘awna ‘being called’ is a circumstantial qualifier that it might decide between them and then a party of them turned away opposed? to the acceptance of its rulings. O Prophet, did you not see the Jews who were given knowledge of the Torah proving your prophethood? (how those who have received the Scripture) were given knowledge about what is in the Torah regarding stoning and other things (invoke the Scripture of Allah) the Qur'an ((in their disputes) that it may judge between them) about stoning the married man and married woman who committed adultery in Khaybar, as is in their Scripture; (then a faction of them) from Banu Qurayzah and the people of Khaybar (turn away) from the judgement, (being opposed (to it) denying that judgement. Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book being called to the Book of God that it might decide between them and then a party of them turned away yatawallā opposedḍ [This means] We have tested you with calling those whom We already know will not answer.

**The invitation to the Book of God for judgement.**

The book is the one they already have, and the demand is to let it decide. The address is to the Holy Prophet and the reference is to the Torah given to the Jews who would have found it enough for them if they were really looking forward to guidance. They are being invited to the Book of Allah to settle their dispute, then a party of them turned away, and they are averse This is because they say: When they are called to refer to the book of Allah, the Torah, so that it can decide about what they differ in, a group of their scholars and leaders turn away, ignoring the judgement of the Torah because it does not agree with their desires. They are the people who turn away ahl al-tawallī from answering ijāba because they have been deprived of the beauty of divine self-disclosure ḥusn al-tajallī by Our prior will irāda.

**The case that brought the verse, and the stoning.**

This was revealed concerning the Jews two of them fornicated and they the Jews asked the Prophet s to adjudicate the case. He ruled that they be stoned but they the Jews refused to do so. When the Torah was brought and consulted the same verdict was found and so the two were stoned but they the Jews became wrathful. Allah mentions after this the rejection of stoning by the Banu Qurayzah and Banu'l-Nadir from among the people of Khaybar, saying: This was revealed about those who committed fornication in Khaybar and the Jews who asked the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, about the legal punishment of fornication . When the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, called the Jews to embrace Islam, al-Nu'man ibn Awfa said to him: The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, entered in on a group of Jews in a Jewish place of study and called them to Allah. Jews contended that they had worshipped the calf for 40 days and so they will incur punishment, if any, for the same period only.

**Their indifference, and the fire they believe will not touch them.**

But they elect to be in-different because they say and believe that the fire of Hell will not touch them except for a few days, after which, according to their supposition, they would be forgiven. This, it has been said, is self-deception caused by what they have been forging for themselves like their belief that they were the progeny of prophets and therefore, they will escape punishment in the fire of Hell. The right thing for them to have done, having claimed that they follow the Torah, is to accept its judgement without hesitation. While dealing with the subject of Jews, as in verses 21-22, the text goes on to censure a particular claim of theirs in the present verse. Let the Scripture of Allah be judge between us .

**The claim about the fire, and the self-deception.**

(This is because they say: "The Fire shall not touch us but for a number of days.") meaning, what made them dare to challenge and defy the truth is their false claim that Allah will only punish them for seven days in the Fire, a day for every one thousand years in this life. (And that which they used to invent regarding their religion has deceived them.) meaning, what caused them to remain on their false creed is that they deceived themselves, believing that the Fire will only touch them for a few days for their errors. " And that which they used to invent in their religion has deceived them How (will it be) when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt (i.e. the Day of Resurrection). (How (will it be) when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt (i. e. the Day of Resurrection).) meaning, what will their condition be like after they have uttered this lie about Allah, rejected His Messengers and killed His Prophets and their scholars who enjoined righteousness and forbade evil? Allah criticizes the Jews and Christians who claim to follow their Books, the Tawrah and the Injil, because when they are called to refer to these Books where Allah commanded them to follow Muhammad , they turn away with aversion.

**The Book they had, and the one guidance of God.**

God’s guidance is one and the same as that revealed to various prophets from time to time in various languages. The same guidance was revealed to the Final Prophet in the form of the Quran. Due to this uniformity in content, recognizing the call of the Quran is not difficult for the People of the Book, i.e. believers in other revealed scriptures. The only difference between the Quranic call and former divine scriptures lies in the fact that the Quran has purified the religion of God of all human interpolations. It is as a result of this mindset that they think that, even if they do not recognize the truth, their salvation is still not at risk.

24.text:
The verse gives the reason for the turning away described before it, and it puts the reason in their own words. "This is because they say" ties the refusal back to a claim they carry, so the turning away is shown to rest on something they believe rather than on a doubt. "The Fire will not touch us except for a few days" states that claim, and the sources weigh the numbers they attached to it, some of them naming forty days and others naming seven, and they read the whole claim as a thing the people made for themselves. "They have been deceived in their faith by their wishful lying" then names the outcome, and the deceiving is credited to what they invented, since a lie a person keeps repeating takes the place of proof and keeps him where he stands. The two halves are joined, the claim and its effect, and the sources read the verse as a censure of a people who had the book and trusted a sentence it does not carry. The verse before described the invitation they refused, and this one shows what stood behind the refusal, while the verse after it asks what their case will be on the day they meet.

**The claim that the Fire will not touch them.**

That turning away and rejection was because they said ‘the Fire shall not touch us except for a number of days’ that is for forty days only the length of time their forefathers worshipped the calf after which it would end; and the lies they used to invent in their saying this have deluded them in their religion wa-gharrahum fī dīnihim ‘it has deluded them in their religion’ is semantically connected to mā kānū yaftarūna ‘the lies which they used to invent’. A group from among the Jews said: the Fire will not touch us except for a limited number of days: seven days of days of the Hereafter-each day equalling a thousand years-as punishment for the days in which our forefathers worshipped the calf. (This is because they say: "The Fire shall not touch us but for a number of days.") meaning, what made them dare to challenge and defy the truth is their false claim that Allah will only punish them for seven days in the Fire, a day for every one thousand years in this life. That because they said the fire shall not touch us except for a number of days ; and the lies they used to invent have deluded them in their religion.

**What the claim was built on, and how it deceived them.**

The claim is treated as a thing they made, and the verse names the effect it had on them. (That which they used to invent has deceived them) their lie about not being punished; it is also said this refers to their claim that punishment shall be postponed (regarding their religion) i.e. their firm adherence to their religion: (And that which they used to invent regarding their religion has deceived them.) meaning, what caused them to remain on their false creed is that they deceived themselves, believing that the Fire will only touch them for a few days for their errors. This belief deceived them and made them bold against Allah and His religion. We have punished them in this world drawing them on by degrees bi-l istidrāj until they [presume to] determine salvation and the lessening of punishment for themselves but they will come to know the doubling of affliction upon them. They think they understand something but they tell a lie. This, it has been said, is self-deception caused by what they have been forging for themselves like their belief that they were the progeny of prophets and therefore, they will escape punishment in the fire of Hell.

**The invitation they were given, and what kept them back.**

While dealing with the subject of Jews, as in verses 21-22, the text goes on to censure a particular claim of theirs in the present verse. They are being invited to the Book of Allah to settle their dispute, then a party of them turned away, and they are averse This is because they say: They turned away from the truth and ignored it because they used to think that the fire of Hell will only touch them for a few days and they will then enter Paradise. But they elect to be in-different because they say and believe that the fire of Hell will not touch them except for a few days, after which, according to their supposition, they would be forgiven. The address is to the Holy Prophet and the reference is to the Torah given to the Jews who would have found it enough for them if they were really looking forward to guidance.

**The day on which the claim will be answered.**

(How (will it be) when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt (i. e. the Day of Resurrection).) meaning, what will their condition be like after they have uttered this lie about Allah, rejected His Messengers and killed His Prophets and their scholars who enjoined righteousness and forbade evil? (That) opposition, denial and punishment (is because they say: The Fire will not touch us) in the Hereafter (save for a certain number of days) about 40 days. Those in error think that [what they have said] is a determination ḥukm.

25.text:
The verse answers the claim of the previous one by moving the whole matter to the day it denied, and it asks the question that the people who made the claim cannot answer. "But how horrible will it be when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt" turns from what they say to what will be done with them, and the question leaves the answer to be felt rather than stated, and the day is described as one that admits no doubt so that the claim of the few days is set against it. "when every soul will be paid in full for what it has done" states the rule of that day, and the word for the full payment carries the sense of a measure filled and nothing held back, so the reward and the requital are given by one rule. "and none will be wronged" closes the sentence and removes the fear that the lessening they invented might be replaced by an unfair addition, since the verse promises that no one is dealt with unjustly and asks no one to expect a favour. The sources bring out the contrast between the claim that the fire would pass quickly and the day that cannot be escaped, and they note that the verse does not answer the claim with an argument but with the plain fact of the gathering. The verses before it described the invitation to the book and the refusal of it, and this verse shows where the refusal leads.

**The gathering on the Day about which there is no doubt.**

But how will it be their predicament when We gather them for a day that is to say on a day of which there is no doubt no uncertainty that is the Day of Resurrection; and every soul from among the People of the Scripture and others shall be paid in full the requital of what is has earned what it has done of good or evil and they that is people shall not be wronged? in that no good deed shall be diminished and no evil deed shall be increased. (How (will it be with them) how shall they act, O Muhammad, (when We have brought them all together) after they die (to a Day) on a day (of which there is no doubt, when every soul) righteous or sinner (will be paid in full what it has earned) of good or evil, (and they will not be wronged) their good works will not be decreased and their sins will not be increased. (How (will it be) when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt (i. e. the Day of Resurrection).) meaning, what will their condition be like after they have uttered this lie about Allah, rejected His Messengers and killed His Prophets and their scholars who enjoined righteousness and forbade evil? But how will it be when We gather them for a day of which there is no doubt and every soul shall be paid in full what it has earned and they shall not be wrongedḍ This address is remarkable because by it He gives information about the imposing grandeur and intensity of the [Day of Gathering] at which point the intellects [of those who turned away] will be perplexed their innermost selves astonished their pretensions cut off their hearts torn from their hidden places and [their souls] will rise to their collar bones. And each person will be paid in full what he has earned And they will not be dealt with unjustly. Every person will be given the reward of his actions according to what he deserves, without there being any oppression by a reduction in good actions or an increase in evil actions.

**The claim they carried, and what meets them.**

But they elect to be in-different because they say and believe that the fire of Hell will not touch them except for a few days, after which, according to their supposition, they would be forgiven. This, it has been said, is self-deception caused by what they have been forging for themselves like their belief that they were the progeny of prophets and therefore, they will escape punishment in the fire of Hell. Then there will be what will meet them from the reckoning and censure al-ḥisāb wa-l- ʿitāb the torment and punishment al-ʿadhāb wa-l-ʿiqāb and the lack of honoring and approval ʿadam al-ikrām wa-l-ījāb etc. The resurrection of the disbelievers will take place on the Day of Gathering while the resurrection of the lovers takes place in the present moment; to explain this fully would take a long time. (This is because they say: "The Fire shall not touch us but for a number of days.") meaning, what made them dare to challenge and defy the truth is their false claim that Allah will only punish them for seven days in the Fire, a day for every one thousand years in this life. (And that which they used to invent regarding their religion has deceived them.) meaning, what caused them to remain on their false creed is that they deceived themselves, believing that the Fire will only touch them for a few days for their errors.

**The honour and the power in the hand of God.**

All kinds of honour and power lie in the hand of God. Those who are considered insignificant by the leaders of the time can be entitled to the highest honour and eminence by the grace of God. In the eyes of God, it is those who regard such attainments as being purely and simply the gifts of God who are deserving of honour and power. In the vaster universe, God daily performs the miracle, on a colossal scale, of bringing darkness after light and light after darkness (i.e. the alternation of day and night). The most undeserving of honour and power are those who consider them to be their own acquisitions. He brings into existence life from dead elements and causes living things to die.

**What the account will be, and whose it is.**

(How (will it be with them) how shall they act, O Muhammad, (when We have brought them all together) after they die (to a Day) on a day (of which there is no doubt, when every soul) righteous or sinner (will be paid in full what it has earned) of good or evil, (and they will not be wronged) their good works will not be decreased and their sins will not be increased. What will be their state and how much will they regret? While dealing with the subject of Jews, as in verses 21-22, the text goes on to censure a particular claim of theirs in the present verse. The address is to the Holy Prophet and the reference is to the Torah given to the Jews who would have found it enough for them if they were really looking forward to guidance.

26.text:
The verse is a prayer that answers the mockery of the people who could not believe the promise given to the Prophet. "Say, O Prophet, O Allah" opens with the command to speak and then turns at once to the name of God, so the answer is not an argument with the mockers but a statement of whose the matter is. "Lord over all authorities" names Him as the master of every kingdom, and the sources read the double form of the address as an honour and a call, and they keep the sense that no authority exists beside His. "You give authority to whoever You please and remove it from who You please" then states what such a lordship does, and the two halves are put together so that the giving and the taking come from one hand, which is the point the promise needed and the mockery could not allow. "You honour whoever You please and disgrace who You please" carries the same rule into honour and disgrace, and the sources place the men and the empires named in the report under these words. "all good is in Your Hands" gathers the whole list under one statement, and the sources notice that the verse names good and does not name evil, and they explain it as the good that every matter ends in when the whole is ordered. "Surely You alone are Most Capable of everything" closes the prayer with the power that makes the promise possible, and it is the same word that ends several of the verses around it. The verse before it described the day of account, and this one shows that the kingdom of the world is in the same hand.

**The prayer that answers the mockery of the hypocrites.**

When the hypocrites of Madīnah heard about it, they found an occasion to ridicule Muslims - 'just look at these people, here they are all scared of the enemy, digging trenches without eating and resting, not knowing for sure if their own lives will be safe, yet they are dreaming of running over Persia, Byzantine and Yemen!' It was in answer to a people so unfair and unjust that Allah Almighty revealed the verse: Appearing in the form of a prayer, this verse so eloquently brings into focus the most perfect power of Allah as it manifests itself in the rise and fall of nations and in the revolutions that rock countries. O Muhammad , while praising your Lord, thanking Him, relying in all matters upon Him and trusting in Him. O Prophet, say in praise of your Lord and in declaration of His greatness: When the Prophet s promised his community sovereignty over the lands of Persia and Byzantium the hypocrites said ‘How preposterous!’ and so the following was revealed Say ‘O God Master of the Kingdom you give the Kingdom to whom You will from among your creatures and seize the Kingdom from whom You will; You exalt whom You will by giving it the kingdom to him and You abase whom You will by seizing it from him; in Your hand in Your power is good that is as well as evil.

**The power that is given and taken, and the honour and the humiliation.**

The two pairs are set in one verse, and the sources read them as one act of disposal. Possessor of the power, You give power to whom You will, and You take power from whom You will, and You endue with honor whom You will, and You humiliate whom You will. (You give power to whom You will, and You take power from whom You will, and You endue with honor whom You will, and You humiliate whom You will.) Allah, to You belongs all authority in this world and the Afterlife. Lead us to goodness (Owner of Sovereignty!) O Master of kings and Owner of sovereignty (Thou givest sovereignty unto whom Thou wilt) i.e. unto Muhammad and his followers, (and Thou withdrawest sovereignty from whom Thou wilt) i.e. from the people of Persia and Byzantium. "0 Allah, 0 Lord of the Kingdom, You give kingdom to whom You will, and take kingdom away from whom You will; and You bestow honour on whom You will, and bring disgrace to whom You will.

**The power in His hand, and the exaltation and the abasement.**

(In Thy hand is the good) exaltation, abasement, sovereignty, spoils, triumph and power. You exalt whom You will by the gleams of the rising Ṭawāliʿ of his intimacy [with You] and You abase whom You will by the night visitors Ṭawāriq of his lower self. Possessor of the power, You give power to whom You will, and You take power from whom You will, and You endue with honor whom You will, and You humiliate whom You will.

**What the promise was, and who made the mockery.**

When the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, conquered Makkah and promised his nation the kingdoms of Persia and Byzantium, the hypocrites and Jews said: 'How far fetched! How on earth can Muhammad conquer the kingdoms of Persia and Byzantium? Are Makkah and Medina not enough for Muhammad that he covets the kingdoms of Persia and Byzantium?' And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse . This verse was revealed about 'Abdullah Ibn Ubayy Ibn Salul, the hypocrite, who said after the Conquest of Makkah: �How on earth can they have sovereignty over Persia and Byzantium?� It is also said that it was revealed about the Quraysh who said: �the king of Persia sleeps on couches made of silk brocade, if you are truly a prophet, show us your dominion?�. Here, enemies of Islam have been warned that they have not learnt their lesson from the rise and fall of past wielders of power for they judge events and personalities from the material angle while the truth is that all powers and governments of the world are in the hands of the most pristine power of Allah, the One in whose hands lies all honour and disgrace. The recurring defeat of the disbelievers of Makkah at Badr and Uhud and their general failure to register any gains in their hostility against Muslims coupled with the growing strength of Muslims and the rise of Islam had made them very nervous, almost reckless. The point worth noting is that a person or a people may regard something as unwelcome, and it may even be so for that particular person or people, but looked at from the wider angle of the whole community of nations, it may not be really evil. The battle is called 'al-Ahzab' in the Qur'an, and 'Khandaq in history, because the Holy Prophet had decided in consultation with his Companions that a khandaq or trench be dug around parts of Madīnah to block the unhindered attack of the enemy during this battle. Then, the digging had to be completed in the shortest possible time which made the noble Companions put in whatever time and energy they had in this effort, so much so that they found it difficult to leave the job and take time for even the most pressing of their needs.

**The kingdom that is seized, and those who held it.**

Allah also granted him extra qualities that no other Prophet or Messenger before him was endowed with, such as granting him (more) knowledge of Allah and His Law, knowledge of more of the matters of the past and the future, such as what will occur in the Hereafter. All kinds of honour and power lie in the hand of God. Those who are considered insignificant by the leaders of the time can be entitled to the highest honour and eminence by the grace of God. In the eyes of God, it is those who regard such attainments as being purely and simply the gifts of God who are deserving of honour and power. O Master of the kingdom there is no associate to You no assistant no helper no companion no partner to You in essence no sharer in the kingdom no competitor in creating. you give the kingdom to whom You will and seize the kingdom from whom You will; ... so that we will know that You are the King. Among created beings the king is he before whom one is humbled and the kingdom that is seized is the kingdom of those who are haughty toward him. [In a similar manner] created beings are beautified tajammul by abasing themselves tadhallul60 before the Real.

27.text:
The verse continues the prayer and gathers three signs under the same hand, moving from the sky to the living things and then to the provision that reaches every creature. "You cause the night to pass into the day and the day into the night" names the turning of the two by which the seasons are measured, and the sources read the passing as one entering into the other, so that the light is extended and the dark is shortened by a measure no one else sets. "You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living" then names the sign of what comes out of its opposite, and the sources fill the words with the cases they saw in them, the bird from the egg, the plant from the seed, the believer from among a people who did not believe, and the seed from the plant in the other direction. "And You provide for whoever You will without limit" closes the verse with the giving that has no measure, and the sources take the word for the unfailing supply that is given without a count and without an end, so the last clause turns the whole list toward the reader's own need. The verses around it speak of the kingdom and the warning, and this one shows the same power at work in the ordinary course of the world, which is why the sources treat it as an argument for the promise it follows. The sources read the whole prayer as a list of things only the Lord of the kingdom can do, and they place the giving of provision last because it is the need that returns every day.

**The night and the day passing into each other.**

You make the night to pass to enter into the day and You make the day to pass to enter into the night each of them increasing by the amount by which the other decreases; You bring forth the living from the dead such as humans and birds from sperm-drops and eggs respectively; and You bring forth the dead the sperm-drop and the egg from the living and You provide with abundant provision whom You will without reckoning’. (Thou causest the night to pass into the day) You increase the length of the day over the length of the night, such that the day is longer than the night, (and Thou causest the day to pass into the night) You increase the length of the night over the length of the day, such that the night is longer than the day. A display of Your power is that You cause the night to become longer by making it enter into the day, and You cause the day to become longer by entering it into the night. You make the night pass into the day such that the authority of the light of unity tawḥīd prevails and nothing remains of the traces of the lower self and its darknesses. You make the day pass into the night so that it is as if the suns of the hearts were eclipsed or as if the night continued and the morning never came.

**The living from the dead, and the dead from the living.**

The sources give the cases they took the words to cover, and the list is long. Mentioned after that is His unrivalled power of 'bringing the living out from the dead' such as, a chick from an egg, or a human infant from the sperm, or a tree from a seed and of 'bringing the dead out from the living' such as eggs from birds and beasts, sperm from humans or fruit from trees and dried grain from plants. (You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living.) means, You bring out the seed from the plant and the plant from the seed; the date from its seed and the date's seed from the date; the faithful from the disbeliever and the disbeliever from the faithful; the chicken from the egg and the egg from the chicken, etc. You bring forth a living creature from a sperm drop, (and Thou bringest forth the dead from the living) and You bring forth a sperm drop from man; it is also said that this verse means: You bring out the living from the dead – as in a believer from a disbeliever and crops from seed – and You bring out the dead from the living – as in a disbeliever from a believer and a chick from an egg. You bring forth the dead from the living such that it is as if the tree of discontent sprouted and blossomed thorns and as if the hopeless found nothing good and could not smell [the fragrance] and their hearts and eyes were confounded just as they did not believe in it the first time [6:110].

**What is given without stint or limit.**

You give provision to whomever You wish, in abundance without any limit or count. And You give wealth and sustenance to whom You will, without limit. It only goes to show that Allah's perfect power exercises absolute control over all phenomena, both physical and spiritual, through which He can make a Muslim out of a Kafir, a perfect believer out of a staunch disbeliever, a scholar out of an ignorant person - if He so wills. It is said that when He said and seize the kingdom from whom You will [3:26] anyone who thinks that he is a king [experiences] a rude awakening from [his] drunken intoxication because he now sees [that] his kingdom is vulnerable to extinction and [he] knows that abasing himself to [God] in preserving His kingdom is worthier than vainglorious delusion and pomposity. (And You give wealth and sustenance to whom You will, without limit.) meaning, You give whomever You will innumerable amounts of wealth while depriving others from it, out of wisdom, and justice. (And Thou givest sustenance to whom Thou choosest, without stint) without measure, exerting power or showing off Your blessings; it is also said that this means: You provide whom You will without reckoning such that there is no labor kadd no exertion jahd no sweat on the brow jabīn and no toil of the right hand yamīn.

**The night and the day, and the living and the dead.**

The second verse demonstrates that Allah controls all spaces and heavenly bodies and employs the sun and the moon to make the days longer than nights and the nights longer than the days at His will and command. If we were to take 'the living' and the dead' in a broad and general sense, this will become inclusive of the learned and the ignorant, the perfect and the imperfect and the believer and the disbeliever (the Muslim and the Kafir). (You make the night enter into the day, and You make the day enter into the night) meaning, You take from the length of one of them and add it to the shortness of the other, so that they become equal, and take from the length of one of them and add it to the other so that they are not equal. Verily, You are able to do all things You make the night to enter into the day, and You make the day to enter into the night, You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living.

**The power and the honour that the prayer names.**

Allah also granted him extra qualities that no other Prophet or Messenger before him was endowed with, such as granting him (more) knowledge of Allah and His Law, knowledge of more of the matters of the past and the future, such as what will occur in the Hereafter. All kinds of honour and power lie in the hand of God. Those who are considered insignificant by the leaders of the time can be entitled to the highest honour and eminence by the grace of God. In the eyes of God, it is those who regard such attainments as being purely and simply the gifts of God who are deserving of honour and power.

28.text:
The verse sets a rule for the community about where its loyalty belongs, and it does so by naming the one case in which a person may act otherwise. "Believers should not take disbelievers as guardians instead of the believers" states the prohibition and puts the word instead at the centre of it, so the fault is not in every dealing but in the exchange of one support for another. "and whoever does so will have nothing to hope for from Allah" then states the loss, and the sources read the phrase as a cutting of the bond, so the person who looks for support elsewhere is left with the support he chose. "unless it is a precaution against their tyranny" makes the exception, and the sources weigh its size in detail, since the words cover what a person does when he is under their hand and fears for himself, and they keep the exception as narrow as the fear that produced it. "And Allah warns you about Himself" then turns the rule into a warning, and the sources explain the strange form as a warning about His anger, since the one who disobeys has to fear what God Himself will do and not only what people will say. "And to Allah is the final return" ends the verse by naming the one to whom the matter goes back, and the sources keep the last clause as the ground of the warning, since the return is the place where the loyalty is examined. The verse before it spoke of the knowledge of what the hearts hide, and this one shows why the hidden loyalty matters. The sources draw from the verse both the rule and its limit, and they keep the two together so that the fear that opens the exception is not turned into a way of living.

**The guardians who must not be taken instead of the believers.**

Let not the believers take the disbelievers as patrons rather than that is instead of the believers — for whoever does that that is whoever takes them as patrons does not belong to the religion of God in anyway — unless you protect yourselves against them as a safeguard tuqātan ‘as a safeguard’ is the verbal noun from taqiyyatan that is to say unless you fear something in which case you may show patronage to them through words but not in your hearts this was before the hegemony of Islam and the dispensation applies to any individual residing in a land with no say in it. (Let not the believers take) the believers ought not to take [the hypocrites:] 'Abdullah Ibn Ubayy and his companions [and] (disbelievers) the Jews (for their friends) so as to become mighty and honourable (in preference to believers) who are sincere. O believers, do not take disbelievers as friends that you love and support instead of other believers: whoever does this will never be helped by Allah in any way. In these verses, Muslims have been instructed not to take disbelievers as their friends.

**The friends who are taken, and the loss that follows.**

(And whoever does that, will never be helped by Allah in any way) meaning, whoever commits this act that Allah has prohibited, then Allah will discard him. (Whoso doeth that) seeking might and honour [by taking the hypocrites and disbelievers as friends] (hath no connection with Allah) has no honour, mercy or protection from Allah (unless (it be) that ye but guard yourselves against them) save yourselves from them, (taking (as it were) security) saving yourselves from them by speaking in a friendly way towards them with, while your hearts dislikes this. Those who take them as friends will find that their bond of love and friendship with Allah has been cut off. On the other hand, there are a large number of verses from the Holy Qur'an, the words and acts of the noble Prophet the practice of the rightly -guided Khulafa' and other revered Companions, which bring to light injunctions and actual modes of dealing with non-Muslims by way of favour, compassion, generosity, sympathy and concern, which has little or no parallel in world history. If we collect all verses of the Qur'an, relating to this subject which appear at several different places and study them all together, we shall find nothing which could bother non-Muslims nor shall there remain any doubt of contradiction in the text of the Qur'an and Hadith.

**The words of the exception, and the fear that stands behind it.**

The exception is read as narrowly as the fear that produced it. The words, ( (unless you guard yourselves against an apprehension from them) appearing in this verse mean this degree of Mudarat which, in other words, means that Muwalat or friendship with disbelievers is not permissible except when you are in a situation where you want to defend yourself against them. Since Mudarat or sympathetic relations somewhat resemble Muwalat or friendship, it was exempted from the category of Muwalat. (Bayan al-Qur'n) However, if you are under their authority and you fear for your lives, then there is no harm if you avoid their harm by being nice to them in your speech and actions on the outside, whilst hating them inside. Let not the believers take the disbelievers as patrons rather than that is instead of the believers — for whoever does that that is whoever takes them as patrons does not belong to the religion of God in anyway — unless you protect yourselves against them as a safeguard tuqātan ‘as a safeguard’ is the verbal noun from taqiyyatan that is to say unless you fear something in which case you may show patronage to them through words but not in your hearts this was before the hegemony of Islam and the dispensation applies to any individual residing in a land with no say in it. And whoever from among you does this he has gone astray from the right path. He set all of them free saying: ‌ which means - Not only that you are being given amnesty this day, we are not censuring you at all for your past tyranny against us either.' When non-Muslim prisoners of war were presented before him, he treated them with such tenderness which many cannot claim to have done even in respect of their children. This too is permissible with all non-Muslims, especially so, when the objective is to present them with some beneficial aspect of the Faith, or when they are guests, or the purpose is to stay safe from any possible harm coming through them.

**The warning about Himself, and the return to Him.**

(And Allah warns you against Himself.) meaning, He warns you against His anger and the severe torment He prepared for those who give their support to His enemies, and those who have enmity with His friends,. (Allah bideth you beware (only) of Himself) regarding the shunning of unlawful killing, unlawful sex, unlawful property, consuming intoxicants, false testimony and associating partners with Allah. Allah warns you of Himself, so fear Him and do not become the subject of His anger by committing sins. And God warns you of Himself, and God is clement to the servants. God warns you He instills fear in you of His Self warning that He may be wrathful with you if you take them as patrons; and to God is the journey’s end the return and He will requite you.

**The love of God, and the intention that is weighed.**

The reality of the servant's faith and the final goal of his traveling on the path of tawḤīd takes him back to God's friendship. Which group is this?' "He said, 'Those who love each other in God.'" It has also been related that God says, "I have obligated My love on those who love each other in Me, sit with each other in Me, visit each other in Me, and spend freely on each other in Me. "O Jesus, if the worship of all the inhabitants of heaven and earth accompanies you in the path of the religion, but you have no love for My friends and no enmity for My enemies, then your worship has been useless and without profit. But friendship with non-Muslims who are at war with Islam is not lawful. In the eyes of God, it is our intention that matters: when our intention is sincere, God does not take us to task for our actions. One should always give proper thought to one’s behaviour, whatever the issue, because one is accountable to God for everything. Now, when it stands established that the purpose of man's life is to obey and worship Allah, the Lord of the worlds, everything else including all affairs of life in this world -- business, government, politics, personal and social relations -- must invariably follow this purpose. Therefore, any deep emotional commitment by a true Muslim in the known forms of love and friendship has to be exclusively for one who is with him all the way in the pursuit of this noble purpose and certainly obedient to what his Lord has commanded him to do.

29.text:
The verse follows the warning about loyalty with a statement that removes the cover from it, since the matter the previous verse warned against is one that a person can hide in his heart. "Say, O Prophet" addresses the Prophet with the words that are to be given to the people, so the sentence is public and its subject is what each one carries inside. "Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it" puts the two cases side by side and gives them the same weight, so hiding the thing changes nothing in the account that is kept of it. "it is known to Allah" states the fact, and the sources bring out the difference between the two words, since one covers what a person keeps back and the other covers what he shows, and both are named as knowledge with God. "For He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" widens the statement from the hearts of people to the whole creation, and the sources read the pair as covering what is hidden and what is seen in everything that exists. "And Allah is Most Capable of everything" closes the verse with the power that can act on what it knows, so the knowledge is not left as a harmless fact, and the verse before it warned about the hidden friendship. The warning is not left as a threat, and the verse names the power that stands behind the knowledge so that a person reads his own heart with fear and with hope. The verses after it go on with the day on which every soul will find what it did.

**What the hearts conceal and what they reveal.**

Say to them ‘Whether you hide what is in your breasts in your hearts of patronage to them or disclose it manifest it God knows it and He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth; and God is Able to do all things and this includes punishing those who patronise them. (Whether ye hide that which is in your breasts) what is in your hearts of hatred and enmity towards Muhammad ﷺ (or reveal it) by showing abuse, defamation and waging war, (Allah knoweth it) Allah will record it and requite for it. Whether you hide within your hearts that which Allah has forbidden, such as befriending the disbelievers, or you reveal the same, Allah knows about it. In the eyes of God, it is our intention that matters: when our intention is sincere, God does not take us to task for our actions.

**The knowledge that reaches the heavens and the earth.**

The two clauses widen the statement from the heart to everything that exists. Allah tells His servants that He knows the secrets and apparent matters and that nothing concerning them escapes His observation. (He knoweth that which is in the heavens and that which is in the earth) of good and evil, what is secret and what is revealed, (and Allah is Able to do all things) regarding the dwellers of the heavens and the dwellers of earth. There is nothing that escapes His knowledge so do not be grieved by any calamity that afflicts you.

**The knowledge of the servants and what they hide.**

And Allah warns you against Himself and Allah is full of kindness with the servants. This Ayah alerts Allah's servants that they should fear Him enough to not commit what He prohibits and dislikes, for He has perfect knowledge in all they do and is able to punish them promptly. He has power over everything and nothing is outside His ability. This verse was revealed about the hypocrites and the Jews. Allah tells His servants that He knows the secrets and apparent matters and that nothing concerning them escapes His observation. There is nothing that escapes His knowledge so do not be grieved by any calamity that afflicts you.

**The friendship that the heart must not carry.**

The words, ( (unless you guard yourselves against an apprehension from them) appearing in this verse mean this degree of Mudarat which, in other words, means that Muwalat or friendship with disbelievers is not permissible except when you are in a situation where you want to defend yourself against them. Since Mudarat or sympathetic relations somewhat resemble Muwalat or friendship, it was exempted from the category of Muwalat. (Bayan al-Qur'n) On the other hand, there are a large number of verses from the Holy Qur'an, the words and acts of the noble Prophet the practice of the rightly -guided Khulafa' and other revered Companions, which bring to light injunctions and actual modes of dealing with non-Muslims by way of favour, compassion, generosity, sympathy and concern, which has little or no parallel in world history. He set all of them free saying: ‌ which means - Not only that you are being given amnesty this day, we are not censuring you at all for your past tyranny against us either.' When non-Muslim prisoners of war were presented before him, he treated them with such tenderness which many cannot claim to have done even in respect of their children. Therefore, any deep emotional commitment by a true Muslim in the known forms of love and friendship has to be exclusively for one who is with him all the way in the pursuit of this noble purpose and certainly obedient to what his Lord has commanded him to do. If we collect all verses of the Qur'an, relating to this subject which appear at several different places and study them all together, we shall find nothing which could bother non-Muslims nor shall there remain any doubt of contradiction in the text of the Qur'an and Hadith. Now, when it stands established that the purpose of man's life is to obey and worship Allah, the Lord of the worlds, everything else including all affairs of life in this world -- business, government, politics, personal and social relations -- must invariably follow this purpose. This too is permissible with all non-Muslims, especially so, when the objective is to present them with some beneficial aspect of the Faith, or when they are guests, or the purpose is to stay safe from any possible harm coming through them. Looking at these clear instructions, non-Muslims who are not aware of the true intention and application of this rule start thinking that the religion of Muslims does not seem to have any place for toleration or bilateral relations or even common courtesy. One of the reasons, a particular one, is that Islam does not see man existing in this world like common animals or jungle trees and blades of grass which sprout, grow, flourish and die and that is the end of it. The question is: °Why has the Qur'an chosen to so strongly block close friendship with disbelievers, so much so that it has not al-lowed it in favour of any disbeliever under any condition? at is the wisdom behind it? It is just not possible for a person who has a definite purpose in life, and who has all his friendships and enmities, agreements and disagreements subservient to this central purpose, to do something like this. A believer treats all human beings with justice and fairness, without differentiating between Muslims and non-Muslims. But friendship with non-Muslims who are at war with Islam is not lawful. When the veil of the divine test is cast aside, the world of the Hereafter will appear before mankind and the fruits of all man’s actions will be before him. Soon He will bring you succor and response and soon the affliction and trial will disappear.

30.text:
The verse turns from what God knows to what every person will see, and it places the good and the evil of a life in front of the one who lived it. "Watch for the Day when every soul will be presented with whatever good it has done" gives the day its name and its work, and the wording places the good in front of the person as something found and not merely remembered. "And it will wish that its misdeeds were far off" then gives the second thing that will meet him, and the sources read the wish as the wish for a distance that cannot be crossed, since the deed is present and the wish has no power over it. "And Allah warns you about Himself" repeats the warning of the earlier verse and stands it here beside the sight of the deeds, so that fear and hope are kept in one place. "And Allah is Ever Gracious to His servants" closes the verse on the kindness that surrounds the warning, and the sources keep both together, since the same verse that makes the account plain names the mercy that calls a person back before the account is taken. The verse before it stated that nothing hidden is outside the knowledge of God, and this one shows the day when that knowledge is set out, while the passage after it turns to the love that has to be proved by following. The sources keep the day and the kindness in one sentence, and they read the verse as a call to prepare for the meeting rather than as a description of what cannot be avoided.

And remember the day every soul shall find what it has done of good present before it and what it has done of evil the last statement constitutes the subject the predicate of which is what follows it will wish that between it and that there were a great distance an extremely lengthy distance so that it the evil could never reach it. (On the Day when every person will be confronted with all the good he has done,) meaning, on the Day of Resurrection, Allah brings the good and evil deeds before the servant, just as He said,. On the Day of Resurrection every person will find the good that he did in front of him, without any deficiency. On the day when every soul shall find the good it has done made present, and the ugly it has done.

On the day when every soul shall find the good it has done made present, and the ugly it has done. It will wish that there were a far interval between itself and that. The two are kept together, since the verse that warns also names the mercy. God warns you of His Self this is repeated for emphasis and God is Kind to His servants. (On the day) the Day of Judgement (when every soul will find itself confronted with all that it hath done) written in its register (of good and all that it hath done of evil) it will also find it written in its register ((every soul) will long that there might be a mighty apace of distance) a long period of time separating them: from sunrise to sunset (between it and that (evil). Allah bideth you beware of Him) upon committing an act of disobedience.

**What the verse asks of the servant, and the state it leaves him in.**

This Ayah alerts Allah's servants that they should fear Him enough to not commit what He prohibits and dislikes, for He has perfect knowledge in all they do and is able to punish them promptly. The words, ( (unless you guard yourselves against an apprehension from them) appearing in this verse mean this degree of Mudarat which, in other words, means that Muwalat or friendship with disbelievers is not permissible except when you are in a situation where you want to defend yourself against them. He set all of them free saying: ‌ which means - Not only that you are being given amnesty this day, we are not censuring you at all for your past tyranny against us either.' When non-Muslim prisoners of war were presented before him, he treated them with such tenderness which many cannot claim to have done even in respect of their children. If we collect all verses of the Qur'an, relating to this subject which appear at several different places and study them all together, we shall find nothing which could bother non-Muslims nor shall there remain any doubt of contradiction in the text of the Qur'an and Hadith. Now, when it stands established that the purpose of man's life is to obey and worship Allah, the Lord of the worlds, everything else including all affairs of life in this world -- business, government, politics, personal and social relations -- must invariably follow this purpose. Therefore, any deep emotional commitment by a true Muslim in the known forms of love and friendship has to be exclusively for one who is with him all the way in the pursuit of this noble purpose and certainly obedient to what his Lord has commanded him to do. Those who take them as friends will find that their bond of love and friendship with Allah has been cut off.

31.text:
The verse takes the claim of love and gives it a test, and the test is the following of the one who brought the message. "Say, O Prophet" puts the words in the Prophet's mouth, and the sources read the address as an answer to people who spoke of their love for God while they kept to their own way. "If you sincerely love Allah" states the claim in the form of a condition, and the sources weigh the word for love as a love that is true in its claim and not only in its words. "then follow me" gives the test, so the following is made the proof of the love and the claim is left without a standing until the proof is given. "Allah will love you and forgive your sins" then states what follows the following, and the sources notice the order, since the love of God for His servant is put after the obedience and not before it, and the forgiveness is the gift that the claim of love could not earn by itself. "For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful" closes with the two names that carry the promise, and the sources read them as the reason the promise stands, since the servant who turns is met by a forgiveness that answers what he did. The verses before this one described what the hearts hide, and the verse that follows turns to those who refuse the obedience. The verse is read as the answer to a claim that was made in words only, and the sources keep the love of God for the servant as the gift that answers the following and never as something earned before it.

**The claim of love and the test it is given.**

This honorable Ayah judges against those who claim to love Allah, yet do not follow the way of Muhammad . In other words, if a person living in the world of today claims that he loves his Creator and Master, then, he must test it on the touch-stone of his obedience to the Messenger, that is, match it against the frequency and quality of where and how he has been following him. This verse was revealed about the Jews who claimed they were the children of Allah and His beloved ones. If you really love Allah, then follow what I have brought, on the inside and the outside. When they said ‘We only worship idols out of our love for God that they might bring us close to Him’ the following was revealed Say O Muhammad ‘If you love God follow me and God will love you meaning that He will reward you and forgive you your sins; God is Forgiving as regards the sins committed previously by one who now follows me; Merciful to him.

**The following that proves the love.**

The sources treat the following as the mark by which the claim is measured. Indeed, Allah does not like whoever does this, even if he claims that he loves Allah and seeks a means of approach to Him, unless, and until, he follows the unlettered Prophet, the Final Messenger from Allah to the two creations: mankind and the Jinn. How much true a person turns out to be in his claim will be visible from how much he makes it a point to follow the noble prophet using the guidance brought by him as the guiding force in his life. "Who ever has fervor in his breast because of these words, say to him: 'Come out in my tracks, for all the work has been made ready in my footsteps. If you love God, follow me.' Whoever wants to serve the threshold of that chieftain of the empire and that center point of good fortune, from now on let him tighten his belt in serving him and assent to be his helper. So the authentic example of a life of God-worship in this world is only such as was handed down to us by His messenger. Now, in these verses, Allah Almighty tells those who claimed that they loved Allah and hoped to be loved by Him above the real criterion of His love. The same test will show that the weaker a person is in his claim, so equally weak he shall be in his obedience to the Prophet . Such people are not true in their claim until they follow the Shari'ah of Muhammad and his religion in all his statements, actions and conditions. ("And forgive you your sins. And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.") meaning, by your following the Messenger , you will earn all this with the blessing of his mission.

**The love of God for the servant, and the forgiveness.**

(If ye love Allah) and His religion, (follow me) follow my Religion; (Allah will love you) He will increase your love (and forgive you your sins) which were committed when you followed Judaism. (Allah is Forgiving) of whoever repents, (Merciful) towards whoever dies in a state of repentance. (Say (O Muhammad to mankind): "If you (really) love Allah, then follow me, Allah will love you...") meaning, what you will earn is much more than what you sought in loving Him, for Allah will love you.

**The prophecy, and the following of the Messenger.**

Affirmed now is the belief in prophethood as well as the necessity of following the Messenger so that we stand informed that the rejection of prophethood or refusal to obey the Prophet is also an act of disbelief (kufr) like the rejection of the Oneness of Allah. This is the Prophet who, if the previous Prophets and mighty Messengers were to have been alive during his time, they would have no choice but to follow, obey him, and to abide by his Law. When this verse was revealed 'Abdullah Ibn Ubayy said: �Muhammad is commanding us to love him as the Christians loved Jesus�, and the Jews said: �Muhammad wants us to take him as a compassionate Lord, just as the Christians took Jesus as a compassionate Lord�. The exalted magnificence of the religion does not fit into the scales of intellect, nor does it come under the confines of substance and accident.'" Our religion is the same as the religion of the 124,000 prophets and messengers. " If everything that is the basis of the religion of the innovators-the substances, accidents, and specific differences of the Kalam experts and the determinations of their intellects-suddenly ceased to be in creation, came to nothing, and entered into the concealment of nonexistence, not an iota of deficiency would reach the threshold of the religion's exaltedness or the gate of the Sun nah's tremendousness. The pearl of prophethood settled down on the carpet of exaltedness and the pavilion of messengerhood was pitched on the face of the earth, its ropes reaching from the east to the west of the world. The mask was lifted from the face of beauty, and because of the scattering of sweet words the world was filled with pearls and gems and adorned and trimmed with the noble character traits of the noble. "Many thousands of years before the existence of the world and of Adam's dust, We gathered together the spirits of the creatures and made a covenant with the spirits of the prophets and messengers: 'Say: The testi mony of the Qur'an contains these words, for He says, "He has set down for you as the religion that with which He counseled Noah" and so on [42:13].

**What the love of God brings with it.**

It is a psychological reality that one who loves someone cannot at the same time love the enemy of the beloved. It is also a fact that when the beloved is a Being who has the status of one’s Creator and Sustainer, then this love will necessarily bring about in the lover the desire to obey that Being in all matters. If the love of God does not produce in him feelings of obeisance to Him, then such a love is false.

32.text:
The verse joins the obedience of God and the obedience of the Messenger in one sentence, and it names what their refusal means. "Say, O Prophet" gives the command its public form, and the sources place it as the answer to those who were arguing about the claim of love in the verse before. "Obey Allah and His Messenger" states the demand and joins the two objects by the same verb, so obedience to the messenger is obedience to the one who sent him, and the sources treat the joined wording as the mark that the two cannot be separated. "If they still turn away" then names the case of those who hear and go back, and the sources keep the turning away as the refusal of the obedience itself and not as a failure of understanding. "then truly Allah does not like the disbelievers" ends with the answer, and the sources read the choice of the word disbelievers as a severity, since the verse does not call them disobedient but names the denial that their turning amounts to. The verse before it gave the test of love, and this one shows what the refusal of the test is called.

**The obedience of God and of His Messenger.**

Say to them ‘Obey God and the Messenger’ as regards the belief in the Oneness of God which he enjoins upon you. (Say: Obey Allah) regarding what He has obligated (and the Messenger) in his practices. Follow Allah and His Messenger by fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions. He commanded them to obedience and then He said But if they turn their backs that is fall short in obedience by opposing [God's command] then God loves not the disbelievers. Allah's Love is Attained by Following the Messenger.

**The disbelievers who turn away.**

But if they turn their backs if they object to obedience God loves not the disbelievers meaning that He will chastise them the third person pronominalisation ‘they’ is replaced by the overt noun ‘the disbelievers’. (But if they turn away) from obeying them, (Lo! Allah loveth not the disbelievers) the Jews and the hypocrites. But if they turn their backs God loves not the disbelievers. He did not say the disobedient ʿāṣūn but rather the disbelievers kāfirūn so the address indicates that He loves the believers even if they are disobedient. If they turn away from the command, then know that Allah does not love the disbelievers who go against His sacred law and the instructions of His Messenger.

**The love that is tested by the following.**

In other words, if a person living in the world of today claims that he loves his Creator and Master, then, he must test it on the touch-stone of his obedience to the Messenger, that is, match it against the frequency and quality of where and how he has been following him. Whether or not a person loves another person, or loves less or more, are questions which cannot be answered precisely. Affirmed now is the belief in prophethood as well as the necessity of following the Messenger so that we stand informed that the rejection of prophethood or refusal to obey the Prophet is also an act of disbelief (kufr) like the rejection of the Oneness of Allah. Indeed, Allah does not like whoever does this, even if he claims that he loves Allah and seeks a means of approach to Him, unless, and until, he follows the unlettered Prophet, the Final Messenger from Allah to the two creations: mankind and the Jinn. It is also a fact that when the beloved is a Being who has the status of one’s Creator and Sustainer, then this love will necessarily bring about in the lover the desire to obey that Being in all matters.

**The Messenger whose example was handed down.**

So the authentic example of a life of God-worship in this world is only such as was handed down to us by His messenger. This is the Prophet who, if the previous Prophets and mighty Messengers were to have been alive during his time, they would have no choice but to follow, obey him, and to abide by his Law. (Say (O Muhammad to mankind): "If you (really) love Allah, then follow me, Allah will love you...") meaning, what you will earn is much more than what you sought in loving Him, for Allah will love you. How much true a person turns out to be in his claim will be visible from how much he makes it a point to follow the noble prophet using the guidance brought by him as the guiding force in his life. Consequently, Allah revealed about their comments:

33.text:
The verse names four houses that God chose and set above the people of their time, and it is placed here to comfort the one who was refused by his own people. "Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah" opens with the first man and the first messenger, and the sources present both as chosen by an act of God and not by any claim their descendants could make. "the family of Abraham" then names the house from which the prophets of Israel came, and "and the family of Imran above all people of their time" completes the list with the house into which the verses that follow will lead, and the sources explain the choice as a preference in prophethood and in the gifts that were placed with them, and they note that it was made above the people of their own time and not above every person in every age. The verse arrives after the command to obey, and it shows that the line of the messengers is itself a matter of God's choosing, so the reader is prepared for the account of Mary and of Jesus that the passage goes on to give.

**Those whom God chose above the nations.**

God preferred He has chosen Adam and Noah and the House of Abraham and the House of ‘Imrān meaning He preferred their selves sc. Allah chose Adam, Nuh (Noah), the family of Ibrahim and the family of 'Imran above the nations Offspring, one of the other, and Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower. (Lo! Allah preferred Adam) with Islam (and Noah) with Islam (and the Family of Abraham) the children of Abraham with Islam (and the Family of 'Imran) Moses and Aaron with Islam (above (all His) creatures) above all the people of their times. He selected all of them and preferred them over all the people of their time. God preferred Adam and Noah and the house of Abraham and the house of ʿImrān above the worlds the seed of one another; God is Hearer Knower.

**Adam and Noah, and what each was given.**

The sources set out what the choosing gave each of them. Allah states that He has chosen these households over the people of the earth. For instance, Allah chose Adam, created him with His Hand and blew life into him. Allah commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam, taught him the names of everything and allowed him to dwell in Paradise, but then sent him down from it out of His wisdom. Allah chose Nuh and made him the first Messenger to the people of the earth, when the people worshipped idols and associated others with Allah in worship. Allah honoured Adam ﷺ, by making the angels prostrate before him; Noah, by making him the first messenger to the people of the earth; the family of Abraham, by placing prophethood in his children; and the family of ‘Imrān, the father of Mary – which is a reference to Jesus ﷺ.

**The family of Abraham and the family of Imran.**

Abraham and ‘Imrān above the worlds by making prophethood reside in them and their progeny. It is also said that Amran is not the father of Moses and Aaron. God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings. He found them so deserving that he showered them with His blessings. These were the people who had no material expectations from their children; their happiness rested upon their children’s dedication and devotion to the cause of God.

**The prophets whose names are given here.**

In these verses a reference has been made to some past prophets to comfort the Holy Prophet since disbelievers did not obey him because they doubted his prophethood. It is for their guidance that names of some past prophets have been cited to help remove such doubts. However, these prophets have been referred to very briefly as the main purpose is to mention Sayyidna Isa which follows immediately because he will come again to this world and will work with the followers of the Holy Prophet therefore, it is necessary for the Muslims to know his identification. God did not grant these blessings to His people for no good reason: It was through their good influence that their children too were in control of their selves and became one with those who truly remembered God: who chose the right way, abandoning the path that leads one astray.

34.text:
The verse closes the list of the chosen houses with a single statement about their line, and it ends with two names of God. "They are descendants of one another" describes the houses named before as one chain, and the sources take the word as covering both the line of the body and the line of the faith, so that the later ones follow the earlier in religion as well as in descent, and the choosing is shown to run through a single thread and not to be scattered among unrelated claims. "And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing" closes the verse with the two names that answer what the people of the book had been saying about themselves, since the claim to be the children of God was heard and the hearts that carried it were known, and the sources keep the two names together as the ground of the choice that was just described. The verse before it named the houses one by one, and this one gathers them into one line, so the reader is prepared for the account of the woman of Imran whose vow opens the passage that follows.

**The houses that are descendants of one another.**

Allah chose Adam, Nuh (Noah), the family of Ibrahim and the family of 'Imran above the nations Offspring, one of the other, and Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower. (They were descendants one of another) some follow the religion of others and the offspring of some are the descendents of others. These prophets and their followers were all part of the same family: declaring Allah’s Oneness and doing good. They passed on noble character and virtues to one another. God preferred Adam and Noah and the house of Abraham and the house of ʿImrān above the worlds the seed of one another; God is Hearer Knower. the seed of one offspring from another of them; God is Hearer Knower.

Allah states that He has chosen these households over the people of the earth. For instance, Allah chose Adam, created him with His Hand and blew life into him. Allah commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam, taught him the names of everything and allowed him to dwell in Paradise, but then sent him down from it out of His wisdom. Allah chose Nuh and made him the first Messenger to the people of the earth, when the people worshipped idols and associated others with Allah in worship. Allah hears the statements of His servants and knows their actions; and therefore chooses whomever He wills.

**The Hearer and the Knower.**

(Allah is Hearer) of what the Jews say: that they are Allah's children and beloved ones and that they follow His religion, (Knower) of their punishment and of whom is following His religion. the seed of one offspring from another of them; God is Hearer Knower. God preferred Adam and Noah and the house of Abraham and the house of ʿImrān above the worlds the seed of one another; God is Hearer Knower.
