However, these prophets have been referred to very briefly as the main purpose is to mention Sayyidna Isa which follows immediately because he will come again to this world and will work with the followers of the Holy Prophet therefore, it is necessary for the Muslims to know his identification. God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings. God did not grant these blessings to His people for no good reason: He found them so deserving that he showered them with His blessings. These were the people who had no material expectations from their children; their happiness rested upon their children’s dedication and devotion to the cause of God. It was through their good influence that their children too were in control of their selves and became one with those who truly remembered God: who chose the right way, abandoning the path that leads one astray.

35.text:
The verse opens the account of Mary with the vow of her mother, and it gives her words in full before it tells what came of them. "Remember when the wife of, Imrân said, My Lord" calls the Prophet and the reader to look at the scene, and the address begins with the Lord and not with the request, which the sources read as the shape of a vow that expects to be heard. "I dedicate what is in my womb entirely to Your service" states what she gives, and the word she uses is the one for a person set free for the service of the house of God, so the child is offered before it is born and offered as a servant and not as a possession. "so accept it from me" is the request that follows the gift, and the sources note that she asks for the acceptance even though the dedication was hers to make. "You alone are truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing" closes the vow with the names of God, and the two are placed there because she is asking about what she cannot see and cannot control, and the sources keep the order, the hearing first and then the knowing, since the prayer is heard before the hidden intention is weighed. The verse before this one gathered the chosen houses into one line, and this one shows the devotion of a household inside that line.

**The vow of the wife of Imran.**

Mention when the wife of ‘Imrān Hanna said after she had reached old age and longed for a child and supplicated to God and sensed that she was carrying child ‘O Lord I have vowed to offer You what is within my womb as a consecration one liberated and delivered from the distractions of this world for the service of Your Holy House in Bayt al-Maqdis. Following this practice, the mother of Sayyidah Maryam made a vow during her pregnancy that she would let the newborn serve Baitul-Maqdis in the way of Allah and that she would not put the child on worldly chores. Remember, O Muhammad (When the wife of Imran) Hannah, the mother of Mary (said: My Lord I have vowed unto Thee that which is in my belly as a consecrated (offering) a servant at the Sanctuary of Bayt al-Maqdis. O Lord, I have made it a duty on myself to fully dedicate my unborn child to You, to worship You and Your House, so accept this act from me. (O my Lord! I have vowed to You what is in my womb to be dedicated for Your services, so accept this from me. Verily, You are the All-Hearer, the All-Knowing.) meaning, You hear my supplication and You know my intention.

**The child set apart for the service of the House.**

The vow belongs to a practice of the earlier prophets, and the sources explain it. In the religious code of earlier prophets, there was a method of worship through which a child, out of one's children, could be freed from all worldly services and devoted exclusively for Allah. Sayyidah Maryam's mother thought that she will deliver a male child. God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings. She vowed to make her child concentrate on worship and serving Bayt Al-Maqdis (the Masjid in Bayt al-Maqdis), when she became aware that she was pregnant.

**The Hearer and the Knower, and the prayer that is heard.**

It is You Who are the Hearer of petition the Knower of intentions. Verily, You are the All-Hearer, the All-Knowing. (Accept it from me. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer) of prayers, (the Knower!) of the answer and of that which is in my womb. You are the One who hears my prayer and knows my intention. It is You who are the Hearer Knower. [3:36] And when she gave birth to her she said Lord I have given birth to a female -and God knew very well what she had given birth to-the male is not as the female.

**Maryam, and the vow that named her.**

From here we learn that a mother holds a certain measure of guardianship over her child in respect of his or her education and training, for Sayyidah Maryam's mother would have never vowed if the mother had no right of guardianship over her child. (And I have named her Maryam,) thus, testifying to the fact that it is allowed to give a name to the newly born the day it is born, as is apparent from the Ayah, which is also a part of the law of those who were before us. And I have named her Mary and commend her to You with her seed to protect them from the accursed Satan. The Real in His prior decree has emancipated such a person from the bondage of preoccupation [with anything other than the Real] in all aspects and states. One set of beings was saved by their story and another was destroyed and expe rienced a trial fitna because of the two of them.

36.text:
The verse tells what happened when the child came, and the whole of it is set inside the difference between what the mother expected and what God had already decided. "When she delivered, she said, My Lord" marks the moment and keeps the address to God, so the disappointment is spoken to Him and not held back. "I have given birth to a girl" states the fact in her own words, and the sources explain that she had hoped for a boy, since the service of the house was given to males and a daughter would not be accepted for it. "and Allah fully knew what she had delivered" steps outside her words to state that the knowledge of God was there before her sentence, and the sources read the clause as the correction of the moment, since what she took for the loss of her vow was what God had chosen. "and the male is not like the female" states the reason for the custom she was following, and the sources weigh whether the word is her own or the answer given to her, and they keep the sense that a girl could not do what the vow had intended. "I have named her Mary" then turns from the disappointment to the child, and the name is given on the day of the birth, which the sources take as evidence for the naming. "and I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed" ends the verse with a prayer that outruns her own life, since the protection is asked for the child and for her children after her, and the sources connect the last clause to the report that Satan touches every new-born except this one and her son. The verse before it told the vow that was made before the birth, and this one shows how it was answered.

**The girl the mother had not expected.**

Sayyidah Maryam's mother thought that she will deliver a male child. I have given birth to a female child, and Allah knew better what she bore, "And the male is not like the female, and I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge with You for her and for her offspring from Shaytan, the outcast. And when she gave birth to her a girl and she had been hoping for a boy since only males were consecrated to the service of God she said apologetically ‘O Lord I have given birth to a female’ — and God knew very well what she had given birth to a parenthetical statement constituting God’s speech a variant reading for wada‘at ‘she gave birth’ has wada‘tu ‘I gave birth’ making these Hanna’s words sc. When the wife of ʿImrān said Lord I have vowed to You what is within my womb as a consecration muḥarraran.

**The male and the female in the vow.**

Of course, a girl does not have the same strength and form as a boy that she had hoped for. (Allah knew best of what she was delivered. The male is not as the female) in service and weakness; (and Lo! I have named her Mary, and Lo! I crave Thy protection for her) I seek for her Your protection and safety (and for her offspring from Satan the outcast) the accursed. ‘and God knows very well what I have given birth to’; the male that she had asked for is not as the female that was bestowed upon her because he is designed for the service of God while she would not be suitable on account of her lesser physical ability her private parts the effects of menstruation on her and so on. (And the male is not like the female,) in strength and the commitment to worship Allah and serve the Masjid in Bayt al-Maqdis. By my life the male is not like the female outwardly but when the Real accepted her every miracle appeared from her.

(And I have named her Maryam,) thus, testifying to the fact that it is allowed to give a name to the newly born the day it is born, as is apparent from the Ayah, which is also a part of the law of those who were before us. ‘And I have named her Mary and commend her to You with her seed her children to protect them from the accursed the outcast Satan’.

**The protection asked for Mary and her offspring.**

In a hadīth it is stated ‘Every new-born is touched by Satan and begins life by crying except for Mary and her son’ as reported by the two Shaykhs Bukhārī and Muslim. One set of beings was saved by their story and another was destroyed and expe rienced a trial fitna because of the two of them. The Real in His prior decree has emancipated such a person from the bondage of preoccupation [with anything other than the Real] in all aspects and states. God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings.

**The child who was dedicated, and the service of the house.**

God did not grant these blessings to His people for no good reason: He found them so deserving that he showered them with His blessings. These were the people who had no material expectations from their children; their happiness rested upon their children’s dedication and devotion to the cause of God. It was through their good influence that their children too were in control of their selves and became one with those who truly remembered God: who chose the right way, abandoning the path that leads one astray. In the religious code of earlier prophets, there was a method of worship through which a child, out of one's children, could be freed from all worldly services and devoted exclusively for Allah. From here we learn that a mother holds a certain measure of guardianship over her child in respect of his or her education and training, for Sayyidah Maryam's mother would have never vowed if the mother had no right of guardianship over her child. (O my Lord! I have vowed to You what is in my womb to be dedicated for Your services, so accept this from me. Verily, You are the All-Hearer, the All-Knowing.) meaning, You hear my supplication and You know my intention. I have vowed to You what is in my womb to be dedicated for Your services, so accept this from me. Following this practice, the mother of Sayyidah Maryam made a vow during her pregnancy that she would let the newborn serve Baitul-Maqdis in the way of Allah and that she would not put the child on worldly chores. She vowed to make her child concentrate on worship and serving Bayt Al-Maqdis (the Masjid in Bayt al-Maqdis), when she became aware that she was pregnant.

37.text:
The verse follows the child from the vow to the sanctuary, and it shows the acceptance of the one and the gift that came with her. "So her Lord accepted her graciously and blessed her with a pleasant upbringing" states that the vow was taken and that her growth was given, and the sources read the acceptance as the good care of God answering a mother's offering, and the pleasant upbringing as a growth made in a way that pleased Him. "entrusting her to the care of Zachariah" then names the man into whose hand she came, and the sources describe the lot that brought him the charge and the plea he made for it, since the daughter of their leader was asked for by the priests and the matter was settled by the casting of pens. "Whenever Zachariah visited her in the sanctuary" describes his visits to the room where she worshipped, and "he found her supplied with provisions, He exclaimed, O Mary" gives the thing he found and his question, and the sources explain that the food came out of its season and that this was the sign that stayed with him. "Where did this come from, She replied" carries the question and her answer, and "It is from Allah" gives the answer in four words, since the source of the gift is named and the means are left where they are, and the sources dwell on the plainness of the reply. "Surely Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit" ends the passage with the same rule that the earlier prayer had named, and it joins the provision given to a girl in a room to the giving of God that no one measures. The verse before described the mother's vow and her disappointment, and this one shows the honour that the daughter was given in her place.

**The acceptance of the child and her upbringing.**

Her Lord accepted the child that is He received Mary from her mother with gracious acceptance and made her grow excellently He made her grow up with excellent character. (And her Lord accepted her with full acceptance) He was good to her and accepted her instead of accepting a boy (and vouchsafed to her a goodly growth) He nurtured her well in worship throughout the years, months, days and hours; (and made Zachariah her guardian) he joined her to him for training. Allah graciously accepted the dedication and brought her up well. Her Lord accepted the child with gracious acceptance and made her grow excellently and Zachariah took charge of her. He caused [Mary] to attain more than what her mother had wished for. It is said that the gracious acceptance was the excellence ḥusn of [God's] care for her in spite of His knowing what would be said about Him because of her for He is not concerned with the shamefulness of the words of enemies. And made her grow excellently until she stood straight in obedience and preferred His good pleasure in every moment and until the fruit from her was such a person as Jesus . It is also said that the gracious acceptance was His causing her to grow preserved [from sin and error] ʿiṣma until she said: (made her grow in a good manner) meaning, made her conduct becoming, her mannerism delightful and He made her well liked among people.

**The care of Zachariah, and how it was decided.**

Her mother took her to the priests the keepers of the Holy House of Bayt al-Maqdis and said ‘This here before you is the dedication I offered’. They competed for guardianship of her because she was the daughter of their religious leader at which point Zachariah said ‘I am most worthy of her for her maternal aunt lives with me’. Thus all twenty nine of them departed to the River Jordan where they cast their quills agreeing that the one whose quill remained fast and floated to the surface of the water would be most worthy of being guardian over her. In order to fulfill her vow, Sayyidah Maryam's mother took her to the Mosque of Baitul-Maqdis and talked to the care-takers and worshippers at the Mosque, Sayyidna Zakariyya being one of them, and. told them that she had vowed to dedicate the child in the service of God and therefore, she could not keep the child with her. Sayyidna Imran was the Imam of this Mosque. He had died during the pregnancy of Maryam's mother, otherwise he would have been the most deserving person to have taken charge of the child, being the father and the Imam of the Mosque. Sayyidna Zakariyya pleaded his bid for custody by saying that his wife was Maryam's aunt and she being next to her mother certainly deserved to keep her. He made the hearts of His pious servants incline caringly to her and put her in the care of the Prophet Zachariah. We should state that in general terms, what Ibn Ishaq said is plausible, and in this case, Maryam was under the care of her maternal aunt. The Two Sahihs recorded that the Messenger of Allah decided that 'Amarah, the daughter of Hamzah, be raised by her maternal aunt, the wife of Ja'far bin Abi Talib, saying,. Zachariah took charge of her and it was part of [God's] gracious acceptance and [His granting her] excellent growth that He made one such as Zachariah among the prophets her guardian and the caretaker and protector of her affairs. He took charge of her and built for her a gallery-room with a ladder in the temple and none apart from him went up to her. Whenever Zachariah went into the sanctuary that is the room the most noble seat in the temple where she was he found her with provisions. She grew up able to sit and walk and Sayyidna Zakariyya put her in a good house adjacent to the Mosque. Finally, everybody agreed to draw lots, which turned out to be fairly strange as it would appear later.

**The food found in the sanctuary.**

He used to bring her food drink and oil and would find her with summer fruits in winter and winter fruits in summer just as God says and Zachariah took charge of her he took her to him a variant reading of kafalahā ‘he took charge of her’ is kaffalahā ‘He God gave Zachariah charge of her’ with Zakariyyā’ or Zakariyyā in the accusative and ‘God’ as the subject of the verb. Every time he entered the Mihrab to (visit) her, he found her supplied with sustenance. (Whenever Zachariah went into the sanctuary where she was) the room where she worshipped, (he found that she had food) the fruit of winter in the summer, such as culms of corn, and the fruits of summer in the winter such as grapes. Whenever Zachariah would enter her place of worship he would find wholesome food there. (He said: O Mary! Whence cometh unto thee this (food)?) how did you get this food out of its season? Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Abu Ash-Sha'tha, Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, 'Atiyah Al-'Awfi and As-Suddi said, "He would find with her the fruits of the summer during winter, and the fruits of the winter during summer. ’ She still very young said ‘From God He sends it to me from Paradise’ ‘Truly God provides abundant provision for whomever He will without reckoning’ without consequence. Among the signs of [God's] gracious acceptance was that she could never be found anywhere except in the sanctuary miḥrāb. (Allah giveth without stint) without pause or measure (to whom He will) in its season or out of it.

**The blessing, and the house that was chosen.**

God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings. God did not grant these blessings to His people for no good reason: He found them so deserving that he showered them with His blessings. These were the people who had no material expectations from their children; their happiness rested upon their children’s dedication and devotion to the cause of God. It was through their good influence that their children too were in control of their selves and became one with those who truly remembered God: who chose the right way, abandoning the path that leads one astray. These were the people who wanted their children to be safe from Satan and join the band of believers.

38.text:
The verse gives the prayer that the sight of the provision produced, and it puts the asking where it belongs. "Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Lord, saying, My Lord, Grant me" ties the prayer to what he had just seen, and the sources read the scene as the reason he made the request at that moment rather than earlier, since he had believed in the power of God but had not seen it act out of season before his own eyes. "by your grace, righteous offspring" states the thing asked for, and the sources notice that he asks for the offspring from the bounty of his Lord and not from his own strength, and that the word he uses for the offspring carries the sense of a good one, since the point of the prayer is the service the child will carry. "You are certainly the Hearer of all prayers" closes the verse with the name that answers the request, and the sources keep the hearing and the answer together, since the one who prays names the God who hears before he names what he wants. The verse before described the food found in the sanctuary, and this one shows what the wonder produced in the man who saw it.

**The prayer that came from what he saw.**

Then when Zachariah had seen this and realised that the One with power to bring something about in other than its natural time is able to bring about a child in old age and with those of his family line all deceased Zachariah prayed to his Lord when he entered the sanctuary to pray in the middle of the night saying ‘Lord bestow upon me from You a goodly offspring a righteous son verily You are the Hearer of You are the One Who answers supplication’. While looking at the first sentence of this verse ‌ ‌ (Thereupon, Zakariyya prayed to his Lord) - we should bear in mind that Sayyidna Zakariyya had no offspring upto that time. When Zachariah saw the food that Allah was miraculously giving to Mary, he became hopeful that Allah would give him a child despite being very old and his wife being unable to bear children. That is when he saw the special gift karāma of God with her he grew increasingly certain and ever more hopeful so he asked for a son in spite of his advanced age. Zachariah saw Mary with summer fruits in the winter and winter fruits in the summer so he asked for a son in his old age so that it might be a sign āya and a miracle muʿjiza.

**The offspring that was asked from his Lord.**

The two causes are named in the sources, and they explain the frame of the request. He had grown old and one usually does not have children in that age, although he firmly believed that Allah, in His ultimate power, could change the usual phenomenon and bless him with an offspring even at his advanced age. But he had not personally witnessed the unusual divine acts - such as he did when he saw unusual and out-of-season eatables provided for Sayyidah Maryam and that was why he did not have the courage to extend his hand of prayer for an offspring. Now when he saw the miracle with his own eyes, he was persuaded for such prayer under the belief that Allah, who can provide a servant with out-of season fruits, would also bless him with an offspring, even in this late age, and so he prayed. The granting of his request was a rupture of ordinary reality naqḌ al-ʿāda.

**The offspring asked for from the bounty of the Lord.**

(Then) at that point (Zachariah prayed unto) and wished from (his Lord and said: My Lord! Bestow upon me of Thy bounty) from You (goodly offspring) a righteous child. It is said that Zachariah asked for a son to help him in obedience and an heir from his progeny in prophethood so that he might uphold the right of God ḥaqq Allāh. Now, should someone try to stop the birth of children, by any means, he will not only rebel against nature but will also deprive him-self of having acted in harmony with the common and agreed practice of prophets The Holy Prophet of Islam has given great importance to the question of marriage and children, so much so that he did not allow anyone to avoid married life and children inspite of his capability, and refused to take such a person as a member of his community of followers.

**Zachariah, and the prayer that was heard.**

(Lo! Thou art the Hearer of Prayer) You are the One Who answers prayers. You hear the prayer of the person who prays to You and You know his condition. At that time Zakariyya invoked his Lord, saying: Then the angels called him, while he was standing in prayer in the Mihrab, (saying): When Zakariyya saw that Allah provided sustenance for Maryam by giving her the fruits of winter in summer and the fruits of summer in winter, he was eager to have a child of his own. "Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya, believing in the Word from Allah, and Sayyidan, and Hasuran, a Prophet, from among the righteous. " Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib said that Sayyid is the scholar and Faqih. 'Atiyah said that Sayyid is the man noble in behavior and piety. 'Ikrimah said that it refers to a person who is not overcome by anger, while Ibn Zayd said that it refers to the noble man. God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings.

39.text:
The verse gives the answer in the middle of the prayer, and the place and the posture are named because they belong to the meaning. "So the angels called out to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary" states that the call came to him where he was and while he was at his worship, and the sources read the scene as the reward of the one who stays at the door, since the answer arrived before he had finished asking. "Allah gives you good news of the birth of John who will confirm the Word of Allah and will be a great leader, chaste" names the child, then the first thing he will do, then the two qualities, and the sources explain the word he will confirm as Jesus, who is called a word of Allah because he was brought into being by the command of God and without a father, and they weigh the word for the leader as the one who is followed in religion, and the word for the one who keeps himself back from what is not lawful, and they set out at length what the second word covers, and they keep the naming of the child beside the news of him, since the news came to the one who had asked and the name was given before the birth. "and a prophet among the righteous" ends the list, and the sources keep the last place for the highest gift, since the prophet is named last and among the righteous, and the passage then goes on to the sign and to the account that follows. The sources keep the angel's call as a call heard while the prayer was still on his lips, and they read the scene as proof that the one who prays is not left without an answer, since the child was named in the answer before the father had asked for a sign. The verse before it gave the prayer of Zachariah, and this one shows how the prayer was answered.

**The call while he stood praying in the sanctuary.**

And the angels namely Gabriel called to him standing in the sanctuary in the temple at worship that anna means bi-anna; a variant reading has inna implying a direct speech statement ‘God gives you good tidings read yubashshiruka or yubshiruka of John who shall confirm a Word being from God namely Jesus that he is God’s Spirit; he is referred to as God’s ‘Word’ because he was created through the word kun ‘Be’; a lord with a following and one chaste forbidden from women and a prophet of the righteous’ it is said that he never sinned and never so intended. The angels called out to him while he was standing in prayer in his place of worship, saying: And the angels called to him as he stood praying in the sanctuary at worship When the petitioner asks and remains at the door the request is granted to him. This alludes to the fact that anyone who needs something from kings should remain at the door until the request is granted. It is said that the ruling of God is such that He only responds to the request of those who embrace service khidma to Him and He casts those who turn away from obedience into the lowliness of estrangement. that God gives you good tidings of John who shall confirm a word from God; a lord and one chaste and a prophet of the righteous. (Then the angels called him, while he was standing in prayer in the Mihrab,) meaning, the angels spoke to him directly while he was secluded, standing in prayer at his place of worship.

**The word of Allah that John will confirm.**

(Allah giveth thee glad tidings of John) a son whose name is John, ((who cometh) to confirm a Word from Allah) Jesus son of Mary that he will be a word from Allah, created without a father, (lordly) who is clement when wronged, (chaste) has no desire for women, (a Prophet of the righteous) among the messengers. Then the angels called him, while he was standing in prayer in the Mihrab, (saying): "Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya, believing in the Word from Allah, and Sayyidan, and Hasuran, a Prophet, from among the righteous. The expression, 'a word of Allah' refers to Sayyidna 'Isa . This term is used for him because he was created, in an unusual manner, simply by the will and command of Allah - without a paternal linkage. He will confirm a word from Allah – which refers to Jesus, son of Mary, because he was specially created by a word from Allah. His saying who shall confirm a word from God Allāh means his con firmation of the word Allāh by which he worshiped Him or that he was brought into being by the word of God.

**The sayyid, the chaste, and what the two words carry.**

The two qualities are explained at length, since the second carries a range of meanings. The second quality of Sayyidna Yahya has been described by the word, 'hasur' translated here as 'abstinent'. Since the quality of abstinence has been mentioned here in a positive frame of reference, it obviously seems to suggest that this is the better way, although ahadith prove the higher merit of living in the bond of marriage. In this situation, the considered opinion is that one whose condition is similar to that of Sayyidna Yahya and who is so absorbed in the thought of his life-to-come that he feels no need to have a wife nor has the time and frame of mind to fulfil the rights of his wife and children, then, for such a person this is the better choice. It is because of this particular reason that ahadith which describe the merit of marriage come up with a restrictive clause as well, that is, which means that one who can marry and is capable of fulfilling the due rights of his wife, should marry, for this is better for him; otherwise, he is not ad-vised to marry. " Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib said that Sayyid is the scholar and Faqih. 'Atiyah said that Sayyid is the man noble in behavior and piety. 'Ikrimah said that it refers to a person who is not overcome by anger, while Ibn Zayd said that it refers to the noble man. He will dedicate himself to worshipping His Lord and will also be a prophet from those who are righteous. It is said that [it means] being protected from the demands of his lower self restrained from that through [his] engagement in exaltation [of God] and seeking to draw near [to Him]. God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings. When we say one abstains from enjoyments of life, the statement includes abstinence even from fulfilling the desires of things allowed, for example, good food, good dress and marital life and things like these. (believing in the Word from Allah) Al-'Awfi reported that Ibn 'Abbas said, and also Al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Ash-Sha'tha, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Ad-Dahhak, and several others said that the Ayah,. (A Prophet, from among the righteous) delivers more good news of sending Yahya as Prophet after the good news that he will be born. (And Hasuran) does not mean he refrains from sexual relations with women, but that he is immune from illegal sexual relations. This does not mean that he does not marry women and have legal sexual relations with them, for Zakariyya said in his supplication for the benefit of Yahya,. It is said his restraint came from being uprooted by the intuitions of realities coming to him such that he no longer had any preference for worldly things.

**The child who was promised among the righteous.**

The Supplication of Zakariyya, and the Good News of Yahya's Birth. When Zakariyya saw that Allah provided sustenance for Maryam by giving her the fruits of winter in summer and the fruits of summer in winter, he was eager to have a child of his own. God did not grant these blessings to His people for no good reason: He found them so deserving that he showered them with His blessings. These were the people who had no material expectations from their children; their happiness rested upon their children’s dedication and devotion to the cause of God. It was through their good influence that their children too were in control of their selves and became one with those who truly remembered God: who chose the right way, abandoning the path that leads one astray. ((Allah) said: "Your sign is that you shall not speak to the people for three days except by signals.") meaning, you will not be able to speak except with signals, although you are not mute.

40.text:
The verse gives the question that the good news produced and the answer that came back to it. "Zachariah exclaimed, My Lord" keeps the address to God, and the sources explain the question that follows as the seeking of a state and not as a doubt, since the man had believed the promise and had seen the power of God at work. "How can I have a son when I am very old and my wife is barren, He replied" states the two causes that stood in the way, and the sources note that he named them in order to learn how the thing would happen rather than to refuse it, and they give the ages and the condition of the wife. "So will it be" gives the answer, and the sources read the short sentence as the promise repeated in the words it had come in before. "Allah does what He wills" closes the exchange with the power that needs no cause, and the sources take the sentence as the reply to the two causes together, since the God who brought the fruit out of its season can bring the child from an age that gives no hope of one. The verse before recorded the prayer, and this one shows the question and the answer that followed the good news.

**The question about the age and the barren wife.**

How shall I have a boy a son when old age has overtaken me that is after I have reached extreme old age 120 years old; and my wife is barren?’ having reached the age of 98. We have already seen that Sayyidna Zakariyya believed in the absolute power of Allah and had seen its manifestation repeatedly and that he had himself made the prayer and knew of its acceptance as well, what then, did he mean by asking: 'how shall I have a boy?' The truth of the matter is that the question asked by him was not be-cause of any doubt in the absolute power of Allah. Quite contrary to this, the purpose of the question was to find out the state in which this was to happen: whether the present extreme old age of both of them would remain just as it was, or would that state be changed. When the angels gave him the good news about John, Zachariah said, ‘O Lord, how can I have a child after I have become old and my wife is unable to bear children? (How can I have a son when age hath overtaken me already) when I am very old (and my wife is barren) and cannot conceive children?

**The reply about the wife who would bear.**

The answer repeats the promise, and the sources read the question as a wish to know the manner. He said ‘So it the matter will be’ with God creating a boy from both of you. ((The angel) answered: So (it will be) as I have told you. The eloquent reply given in (That is how Allah does what He wills) makes it clear that they were to remain at the same age and that they would have an offspring in that very state. ’ Allah replied to him that the example of the creation of John, in spite of his old age and his wife being barren, is like that of the creation of anything that Allah wishes to create, even though it is out of the ordinary. So it was said to him No not through these means for both you and your wife have suffered loneliness together so the good news of the son is for both of you. It is said that there was a long time between his petition and the reply and because of that he said How shall I have a boyḍ It may mean that he said By what right would I receive a response [to my prayer] if not by Your favorḍ 93 It may mean that he said How shall this be: by adoption or sexual procreationḍ It may mean that [he questioned] whether this was to be from a woman other than his wife since she was [also] of advanced age [that is] from taking a slave as a concubine.

**The will of Allah that needs no cause.**

‘God does what He will’ nothing can prevent Him therefrom and in order to manifest this great power he was inspired with the question so that he would be answered through it this great power. This is because Allah has power over everything and does whatever He wills in His wisdom and knowledge. "Allah gives you glad tidings of Yahya, believing in the Word from Allah, and Sayyidan, and Hasuran, a Prophet, from among the righteous. When Zakariyya saw that Allah provided sustenance for Maryam by giving her the fruits of winter in summer and the fruits of summer in winter, he was eager to have a child of his own. God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings. God did not grant these blessings to His people for no good reason: He found them so deserving that he showered them with His blessings. 42.text:
The verse turns from Zachariah to Mary and gives the address that the angels brought to her, and the three statements it carries are placed in an order. "And remember when the angels said, O Mary" introduces the scene as a reminder, and the sources note that the speech was heard by her, whether the speaker was seen or only heard as a voice. "Surely Allah has selected you, purified you" gives the first two acts, and the sources read the choosing as the gift of faith and worship set in her, and the purifying as a removal from what is unclean and from the blame that is laid on women, so the two are kept apart and yet held together. "and chosen you over all women of the world" completes the address with the preference, and the sources read it as the women of her own time, and they record the hadith that names other women among the foremost, so that no contradiction is left in the words. The verse before described the sign given to Zachariah, and this one opens the sequence of the addresses to Mary that the passage goes on to give, and the three statements are kept in that order wherever the sources take them up.

**The address of the angels to Mary.**

And mention when the angels namely Gabriel said ‘O Mary God has preferred you He has elected you and made you pure of the touch of men; He has preferred you above all women of the worlds that is the inhabitants of your time. And when the angels said O Mary God has preferred you and made you pure; He has preferred you above all women of the worlds. It is possible that this was the beginning of a message from the angels to Mary elevating her state. Gabriel (said: O Mary! Lo! God has preferred you by your being favored and singled out from among your kind and peers and made you pure from what is indecent and sinful with a beautiful immunity and [pure] from having physical contact with men. The point of repeating the mention of her being preferred is first He has chosen you through special gifts position and an exalted state ; and second He has chosen you to bear Jesus without a father and no woman can ever be compared to you until the Day of Resurrection.
