44.text:
The verse closes the account of the house of Imran by naming the source of the story, and the two denials at its end are the proof that the telling could not have been borrowed. "This is news of the unseen that We reveal to you O Prophet" states where the account came from, and the sources read the sentence as an argument for the prophethood, since the events belong to a remote past that no one in the Prophet's own time could have seen or heard or read. "You were not with them when they cast lots to decide who would be Mary's guardian" takes the reader to the dispute itself, and the sources spell out the scene, the pens thrown into the water and the prior agreement that the pen which flowed against the current would name the winner, and they keep the custodianship as the prize the disputants sought, since the house of God was in the care of the men of the line. "nor were you there when they argued about it" gives the quarrel that came before the lots, and the sources keep the two together because the casting settled a claim that the disputants had already pressed on one another, and they read the whole scene as one that a man of that time could not have witnessed. The sentence answers the doubt of the listener who might think the story had been learned from the people of the Book, and the sources read the passage as a sign given to the one who had no way of learning such things by any ordinary means. The verse before gathered the chosen houses into one line, and this one shows how the news of them reached the Prophet.

**The news of the unseen that We reveal.**

That which has been mentioned of the matter of Zachariah and Mary is of the tidings of the Unseen of the news of what was unknown to you. (This is a part of the news of the Ghayb which We reveal.) "and narrate to you (O Muhammad), " (This) which I mentioned of the story of Mary and Zachariah (is of the tidings of things hidden) of the things that were unknown to you, O Muhammad. The story of Zachariah and Mary is one of the reports of [the Ghaib] which I reveal to you, O Messenger. That is We have told you [Muḥammad] of these stories and have spoken with you about their meanings.

**The Prophet was not present at the casting of lots.**

We reveal it to you O Muhammad for you were not with them when they were casting quills in the water drawing their lots so that it be manifested to them which of them should have charge of which of them should bring up Mary; nor were you with them when they were disputing about the custodianship of Mary such that you might have known it and related it; but truly you know it only through revelation. You were not with them, when they cast lots with their pens as to which of them should be charged with the care of Maryam; nor were you with them when they disputed. (You were not with them, when they cast lots with their pens as to which of them should be charged with the care of Maryam; nor were you with them when they disputed.) meaning, "You were not present, O Muhammad, when this occurred, so you cannot narrate what happened to the people as an eye witness. Rather, Allah disclosed these facts to you as if you were a witness, when they conducted a lottery to choose the custodian of Maryam, seeking the reward of this good deed." (Thou wast not present with them) with the Rabbis (when they threw their pens) in the flow of water ((to know) which of them should be the guardian of Mary) to train her, (nor wast thou present with them when they quarrelled (thereupon) each giving argument for his better claim to be Mary's guardian. They eventually decided to draw lots by throwing their pens, and the pen of Zachariah ﷺ won. The text very eloquently states that the Holy Prophet was not there to see them drawing lots (by throwing their reed pens in water,. based on prior agreement that the owner of the pen which flows against the current shall be the winner), nor was he present on the scene when they were initially quarreling about the custody of Maryam before agreeing upon the drawing of lots.

**The argument over who would raise Mary.**

This verse presents an argument to prove the prophethood of Sayyidna Muhammad by referring to happenings in the lives of Sayyidna Zakariyya and Sayyidah Maryam. These took place in the remote past and there is no likelihood of their being seen or heard or read, specially so, by the Holy Prophet which by itself proves that his being so informed of the unknown was beyond the ordinary course of learning. We reveal it to you for you were not with them when they were casting quills which of them should have charge of Mary; nor were you with them when they were disputing. They were responsible for taking care of Bayt Al-Maqdis (the Masjid) at that time, just as there were those who took care of the Ka'bah. Maryam's mother said to them, 'Take this child whom I vowed [to serve the Masjid], I have set her free, since she is my daughter, for no menstruating woman should enter the Masjid, and I shall not take her back home.' They said, 'She is the daughter of our Imam,' as 'Imran used to lead them in prayer, 'who took care of our sacrificial rituals.' Zakariyya said, 'Give her to me, for her maternal aunt is my wife.' They said, 'Our hearts cannot bear that you take her, for she is the daughter of our Imam.' So they conducted a lottery with the pens with which they wrote the Tawrah, and Zakariyya won the lottery and took Maryam into his care."

**The drawing of the lot among the custodians.**

The rule governing Qur'ah (to the drawing of lots) according to Hanafi jurists, is that Qur'ah (drawing of lots) cannot be given a decisive role in determining the rights known and fixed in Islamic Law. This is permissible because this was permissible even with-out having to draw lots by a mutual agreement of the parties concerned or by a decree of a judge. In other words, it can be said that in a situation where the rights of all parties are equal and the purpose of the lot is only to allocate equal portions to each of them and to decide as to which portion is for whom, then drawing a lot is permissible.

**The blessing given to the descendants of Abraham.**

Hence, the truth is that this information was revealed to him as part of the message he gave to others. God blessed Zachariah (Zakariyya) with an offspring in his old age; provided sustenance to Mary in her shrine; created Jesus without a father, and brought into being chaste and upright people who were descendants of Abraham, so that they could be chosen to communicate the message of God to human beings. He found them so deserving that he showered them with His blessings. These were the people who had no material expectations from their children; their happiness rested upon their children’s dedication and devotion to the cause of God. These were the people who wanted their children to be safe from Satan and join the band of believers. It was through their good influence that their children too were in control of their selves and became one with those who truly remembered God: who chose the right way, abandoning the path that leads one astray. Such are the people whom God provides for out of His special mercy, and who have His special blessings showered upon them.

45.text:
The verse turns from Zachariah to Mary and gives the announcement that answers her prayer, and the whole of it is a naming of the child before he is born. "Remember when the angels proclaimed, O Mary" opens the address and fixes the speaker as the angels, and the sources name Gabriel among them, and they read the call to her as an honour, since she is addressed by name and not through another. "Allah gives you good news of a Word from Him" states what is given to her, and the sources explain the word as the son who would come into being by the command of God, and they read the phrase as the announcement of a birth without a father, so that the child is called a word of Allah because he was brought into being by the command and not by any cause. "his name will be the Messiah, Jesus" gives the name and then the title, and the sources spell out what the title carries, the one anointed and the one who travels, and they keep the name beside the title because both belong to the same child. "son of Mary" gives the line through the mother alone, and the sources read it as the sign of the fatherless birth, since the child is named after her and not after any man. "honoured in this world and the Hereafter" states the rank, and the sources read the honour of this world as the prophethood and the good standing among the people and the honour of the last life as the intercession and the high place with God. "and he will be one of those nearest to Allah" closes the announcement with the highest of the gifts, and the sources keep the honours in the order given, the world first and then the last life, since the nearness to God is the greater of the two. The passage then goes on to answer the question that the announcement raised in her.

**The address of the angels to Mary.**

Mention when the angels namely Gabriel said ‘O Mary God gives you good tidings of a Word from Him that is a boy whose name is the Messiah Jesus son of Mary He addresses her attributing him to her in order to point out that she will give birth to him without a father for the custom is to attribute the child to its father honoured shall he be in this world through prophethood and the Hereafter through his intercession and the high stations al-darajāt al-‘ulā cf. When the angels said, "O Mary, surely God gives thee the good news of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, celebrated in this world and the next, and one of those given proximity. " In this verse the God of the universe, the enactor of the world's folk, the assigner of daily provi sions to the servants, the bestower of bounty and the lovingly kind, the caresser of the friends, caresses Mary and honors her. With this honoring He gives her excellence over the women of the world and separates her from all of them. First, He calls her with the vocative of honor, saying "O Mary.

**The good news of a Word from Him.**

This Ayah contains the glad tidings the angels brought to Maryam that she would give birth to a mighty son who will have a great future. ((Remember) when the angels said: "O Maryam! Verily, Allah gives you the glad tidings of a Word from Him,) a son who will come into existence with a word from Allah, 'Be', and he was. Gabriel (said: O Mary! Allah giveth you glad tidings of a Word from Him) of a son who shall come into being by means of a Word from Allah, (whose name is the Messiah) because he travels from one country to another; it is also said: the Messiah means the king, (Jesus, son of Mary, illustrious in the world) he has standing and position amidst people in the life of this world (and the Hereafter) he has standing and position with Allah, (and one of those brought near) unto Allah in the Garden of Eden. Allah used the word 'create' here instead of the word 'does' as in the tale about Zakariyya [3:40], to eradicate any evil thought concerning 'Isa. Allah next emphasized this fact when He said,.

**The name of the child, and the honor that was given him.**

(His name will be Al-Masih, 'Isa, the son of Maryam) and he will be known by this name in this life, especially by the believers. 'Isa was called "Al-Masih" (the Messiah) because when he touched (Mash) those afflicted with an illness, they would be healed by Allah's leave. (Believing in the Word from Allah.)[3:39], according to the majority of the scholars. (Held in honor in this world and in the Hereafter, and will be one of those who are near to Allah.) meaning, he will be a leader and honored by Allah in this life, because of the Law that Allah will reveal to him, sending down the Scripture to him, along with the other bounties that Allah will grant him with. 'Isa will be honored in the Hereafter and will intercede with Allah, by His leave, on behalf of some people, just as is the case with his brethren the mighty Messengers of Allah, peace be upon them all. (He will speak to the people, in the cradle and in manhood,) calling to the worship of Allah Alone without partners, while still in the cradle, as a miracle from Allah, and when he is a man, by Allah's revelation to him. He will have a high rank in this world and the Afterlife and he will be one of those who are made close to Allah. His extraordinary birth and his performance of extraordinary miracles were meant to convince the Jews of his messengership (i.e. that he had been sent by God) and that he was speaking on behalf of God. The Jews were chosen by God for the special mission of being the bearers of divine guidance so that, along with following the path of God, they should also communicate this guidance to others. God then took away this trust from them and gave it to the other branch of Abraham’s dynasty, the Banu Isma‘il. Jesus Christ was sent by God for this purpose. Before the enforcement of this decree, it was necessary to prove to them that they were no longer to be trusted. Abū Yazīd BasṬāmī said, "God stood me before Him in a thousand standing places, presenting the empire to me, but I was saying, 'I do not desire it.' In the last standing place He said to me, 'O Abū Yazīd, what do you desire?' I said, 'I desire not to desire,'" that is, I desire what You desire. "Then He said, 'You are My servant in truth.'" Even if you do not have the gall to speak with God like Abū Yazīd, you are not too small to present your need to Him, to show Him your burning and hope, and to say, "O Lord, a name and mark is enough for me! The previous verse appeared parenthetically between the present verses 45 - 46 and verses 42 - 43 and the purpose was to affirm the prophethood of Sayyidna Muhammad . The present verse resumes with the story of Sayyidah Maryam which actually pre-pares the ground for a fuller account of the birth, mission and miracles of Sayyidna 'Isa .

46.text:
The verse carries the last of the qualities announced to Mary, and it places the speech of the child beside his standing among the righteous as one of the signs given to her. "And he will speak to people in his infancy and adulthood and will be one of the righteous" states the wonder and then the rank of the one who works it, and the sources read the first half as speech in the cradle, while he was still an infant and before the age of speech, and the second half as speech in his manhood, when he would call the people to the worship of God. The sources keep the two together because the early speech was a sign given to one who could not yet speak, and the later speech was the ordinary work of a prophet sent to a people, and they place both beside the closing word about the righteous, which they read as the good in word and in deed. The sources also weigh the mention of the middle age, since the child would be raised before he reached it, and they read the verse as a proof that he would come back in that age and speak to the people again. The verse before named the child and his honour, and this one names the sign that marked him from the first day.

**The speech in the cradle.**

He shall speak to mankind in the cradle that is to say as a child before the age of speech and in his manhood and he is of the righteous’. One of the qualities of Sayyidna 'Isa mentioned in this verse is that 'he shall speak in the cradle' which means that he will speak while still a child, although no child has the ability to do so. When soon after the birth of infant Jesus as mentioned in another verse, people chided Sayyidah Maryam on the basis of a false accusation, this new-born infant, Sayyidna Isa spoke up, saying: (He will speak to the people, in the cradle and in manhood,) calling to the worship of Allah Alone without partners, while still in the cradle, as a miracle from Allah, and when he is a man, by Allah's revelation to him. This child will miraculously speak to people when he is a small baby, as well as when he grows up and becomes a man. (He will speak unto mankind in his cradle) in the lap of his mother, saying:

**The speech in his manhood.**

Then following immediately, it was said that he will also talk to people when he will be in the later middle of his age (kahl). But, speaking to people during one's middle age is very normal, something everyone does no matter whether he is a Muslim, or a non-Muslim, learned or illiterate. One answer to this question appears in Bayan al-Qur'an by Maulana Ashraf Thanavi who says that the real purpose here is to particularly focus onthe miraculous nature of meaningful infant speech. The reference to the speech in the middle age is there to indicate that his childhood speech too would not be the usual baby-talk, rather it would be rational, even learned and eloquent, as man does in his advanced years. If we were to look into the true historical background of Sayyidna Isa we would discover that this reference to him as speaking to people in his middle age provides a great standing argument in favour of the Islamic position which, according to the Qur'anic belief, is that Sayyidna Isa has been raised alive onto the heavens. Middle age, kohl in Arabic, was something he never reached during his life in this world. I am the servant of Allah and His Messiah (and in his manhood) after he reaches 30 years old, saying that he is a prophet, (and he is of the righteous) of the messengers. He told her that he would live in such as way that he shall speak to mankind as a young child and in his manhood and that the deception of [his] enemies would not affect him. It is said in manhood [means] after his descent from the heavens. (He will speak to the people, in the cradle and in manhood,) calling to the worship of Allah Alone without partners, while still in the cradle, as a miracle from Allah, and when he is a man, by Allah's revelation to him. He will tell them what is best for them in their religious and worldly affairs.

**The honor that he was given, and the righteous.**

(And he will be one of the righteous.) in his statements and actions, for he will possess, pure knowledge and righteous works. He will also be one of those who are righteous in their words and actions. (Held in honor in this world and in the Hereafter, and will be one of those who are near to Allah.) meaning, he will be a leader and honored by Allah in this life, because of the Law that Allah will reveal to him, sending down the Scripture to him, along with the other bounties that Allah will grant him with. 'Isa will be honored in the Hereafter and will intercede with Allah, by His leave, on behalf of some people, just as is the case with his brethren the mighty Messengers of Allah, peace be upon them all.

**The proof that her son would speak.**

It is said that He fortified her heart by informing her that while she herself would hold her tongue regarding her innocence [after the birth] God would cause Jesus to speak [as a child] as proof of her sincerity and exalted honor. It is said that He informed her that whoever succumbs to the over whelming force of the divine power qudra and ends up before His ruling ḥukm will encounter miracles of that power the likes of which no one has experienced. Mary had surely lived for a long time with an excellent reputation and was well-known as a chaste [woman] but then [God] caused confusion about her situation [when she] appeared in a state deemed blame worthy by people. He told her that he would live in such as way that he shall speak to mankind as a young child and in his manhood and that the deception of [his] enemies would not affect him. When the angels said O Mary God gives you good tidings of a word from Him whose name is the Messiah Jesus son of Mary honored shall he be in this world and the hereafter and of those brought close. He shall speak to mankind in the cradle and in his manhood and he is of the righteous.

47.text:
The verse gives the question that the announcement raised and the answer that settled it, and the two together carry the teaching about how God brings a thing into being. "Mary wondered, My Lord" keeps her words in the form of an address, and the sources read the wonder as the surprise of a woman who had never known a man, and they note that the question came from not knowing how the promise would be kept and not from any doubt about the promise itself. "How can I have a child when no man has ever touched me" states the difficulty in her own words, and the sources keep the two ways in which a child can come, the lawful and the unlawful, and they read her words as a denial of both. "An angel replied" names the speaker and turns the verse from the question to the comfort. "So will it be" answers with the decree alone, and the sources read the words as the announcement that the child would be created without a father, since the command of God is not bound by the causes that bind other births. "Allah creates what He wills" gives the ground of the answer, and the sources read it as the will that needs no means and no cause, since it is enough by itself to bring a thing into existence. "When He decrees a matter" narrows the thought to the moment of the decree, and the sources keep the decree as a ruling that comes to pass as it is wished, so that nothing stands between the will and the thing willed. "He simply tells it, Be" names the word that carries the creation, and the sources weigh the command as the only instrument, so that the thing comes into being with the word and not before it. "And it is" closes the verse with the instant answer of the command, and the sources keep the two halves, the telling and the being, as one act. The verse before gave the announcement, and this one gives the question it raised and the answer that resolved it.

**The child that no man had touched.**

Mary was surprised that she was to have a child without a husband and said in astonishment: How can I have a child when no man has come near me in a lawful or unlawful way? The glad tidings given by the angel (verse 46) regarding the birth of Sayyidna Isa without a father surprised Sayyidah Maryam as she was a virgin. Would that be a Divine miracle or would she be asked to marry a man? (How can I have a child) how is it possible for me to have a child (when no mortal hath touched me?) lawfully or unlawfully? Mary said, "How can I have a son while I did not marry, nor intend to marry, nor am I an indecent woman, may Allah forbid?

**The answer that the child would come without a father.**

She said ‘Lord how shall I have a child when no mortal has touched me?’ neither through conjugality or otherwise; He said the command ‘It is such that God will create from you a child without a father. The Divine answer eliminates the latter possibility. Gabriel (said: So (it will be) as I have told you. Just as you witnessed the appearance of things contrary to ordinary reality in the provision We gave [to you] likewise We will break with ordinary reality by creating a son without a man having touched [you]. Just as Allah will create a child for you without a father, He creates whatever He wishes even though it may be out of the ordinary. (Held in honor in this world and in the Hereafter, and will be one of those who are near to Allah.) meaning, he will be a leader and honored by Allah in this life, because of the Law that Allah will reveal to him, sending down the Scripture to him, along with the other bounties that Allah will grant him with. 'Isa will be honored in the Hereafter and will intercede with Allah, by His leave, on behalf of some people, just as is the case with his brethren the mighty Messengers of Allah, peace be upon them all. (His name will be Al-Masih, 'Isa, the son of Maryam) and he will be known by this name in this life, especially by the believers. 'Isa was called "Al-Masih" (the Messiah) because when he touched (Mash) those afflicted with an illness, they would be healed by Allah's leave. (He will speak to the people, in the cradle and in manhood,) calling to the worship of Allah Alone without partners, while still in the cradle, as a miracle from Allah, and when he is a man, by Allah's revelation to him. (And he will be one of the righteous.) in his statements and actions, for he will possess, pure knowledge and righteous works. Verily, Allah gives you the glad tidings of a Word from Him, his name will be Al-Masih, 'Isa, the son of Maryam, held in honor in this world and in the Hereafter, and he will be one of those who are near to Allah. This Ayah contains the glad tidings the angels brought to Maryam that she would give birth to a mighty son who will have a great future. His extraordinary birth and his performance of extraordinary miracles were meant to convince the Jews of his messengership (i.e. that he had been sent by God) and that he was speaking on behalf of God. Before the enforcement of this decree, it was necessary to prove to them that they were no longer to be trusted. God then took away this trust from them and gave it to the other branch of Abraham’s dynasty, the Banu Isma‘il. Then a time came when they were no longer worthy of being the bearers of divine guidance.

**The thing that comes into being at the word.**

Not restricted by it, 'Allah creates what He wills', that is, His will is all sufficient to bring some-thing into existence. It is only His command "be" which makes things come into existence. When Allah wishes for something, He says ‘Be’ and it is. Producing [things] from the beginning and bringing [them] forth are not difficult for Him. When He decrees a thing willing its creation He says to it only “Be” and it is that is and ‘he is’. (When He has decreed something, He says to it only: "Be! and it is.) meaning, what Allah wills, comes into existence instantly and without delay. Allah used the word 'create' here instead of the word 'does' as in the tale about Zakariyya [3:40], to eradicate any evil thought concerning 'Isa. (And Our commandment is but one as the twinkling of an eye.)[54:50], meaning, "We only issue the command once, and it comes into existence instantly, as fast as, and faster than, a blink of the eye.

**The decree and the word Be.**

(Allah createth what He will. If He decreeth a thing) if He wills to create a son from you without a father, (He saith unto it only: Be! and it is) a son without a father. When He decrees a thing that is He desires a ruling ḥukm to come to pass He says to it only: 'Be' and it is. When they began to blame her God caused Jesus to speak when he was [only] one day old; [he] said I have come to you with a sign from your Lord [3:49]. ((Remember) when the angels said: "O Maryam! Verily, Allah gives you the glad tidings of a Word from Him,) a son who will come into existence with a word from Allah, 'Be', and he was. (No infant spoke in the cradle except three, 'Isa, the boy during the time of Jurayj, and another boy.) "He will speak to the people, in the cradle and in manhood, and he will be one of the righteous.

48.text:
The verse names the gifts that would be given to the child, and it places them before the commission that he would carry, so that the teaching comes first and the message follows. "And Allah will teach him writing and wisdom" states the first gift, and the sources read the writing as the Book that is set down and the wisdom as the knowledge that goes with it, and they keep the two together because the one who is taught is fitted for the office that comes next. "the Torah and the Gospel" gives the two books by name, and the sources read the first as the book sent down to Moses and the second as the book that would be sent down to the child himself, and they note that he would carry both in memory and in understanding. The sources also read the whole verse as the answer to the doubt of the Christians about his station, since the gift of knowledge is placed in the same sentence as his birth, and they keep the teaching and the message in one line of gifts so that the two are seen to come from the same hand. The verse before gave the answer about how the child would come, and this one names what he would be given.

**The teaching that was placed in him.**

And We will teach him read nu‘allimuhu or yu‘allimuhu ‘He will teach him’ the Book that is script wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel. (And He will teach him the Scripture) the Scriptures of [past] prophets; as it is said: writing (and wisdom) the lawful and the prohibited; as it said this means: the wisdom of the prophets who preceded him, (and the Torah) in the womb of his mother (and the Gospel) after he came out of his mother's womb. Allah will teach him to say and do things correctly; and He will teach him the Torah that He had revealed to Moses ﷺ and the Gospel which He will reveal to him. And He will teach him the Book and Al-Hikmah, and the Tawrah and the Injil And will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel (saying): Verse 48 recounts the august virtues of Sayyidna Isa who would be born blessed with the honour of learning from Allah:

**The Book and the wisdom.**

Scriptures, Wisdom and specially the Torah and the Injil; and that he will be sent as a Messenger of Allah to all of the Children of Isra il. The Tawrah is the Book that Allah sent down to Musa, son of 'Imran, while the Injil is what Allah sent down to 'Isa, son of Maryam, peace be upon them, and 'Isa memorized both Books. The message he will carry to them will be his argument in favour of his prophethood. (And will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel) means, that Allah will send 'Isa as a Messenger to the Children of Israel, proclaiming to them,.

**The Torah and the Injil that were sent down.**

Verse 50 says that Sayyidna Isa will declare that he has come to confirm Torah which was revealed before his coming and to make lawful what remained unlawful for them in the law of Moses. This means that the unlawfulness of some things in the earlier code would stand abrogated by the new one, (that of Sayyidna Isa) whose station of prophethood was the conclusive argument for that claim of abrogation. Once his prophethood is established, verse 51 states that Sayyidna Isa will ask them to beware of any contravention of Divine commandments, fear Allah, and follow his teachings in matters of religion which, in a nutshell, are that 'Allah is my Lord and your Lord' (the ultimate in belief) and 'Worship Him' (the ultimate in deeds). And He will teach him the Book and Al-Hikmah, and the Tawrah and the Injil And will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel (saying): The Tawrah is the Book that Allah sent down to Musa, son of 'Imran, while the Injil is what Allah sent down to 'Isa, son of Maryam, peace be upon them, and 'Isa memorized both Books. Because it was in God's knowledge that the Christians would exaggerate concerning him, the Lord of the Worlds gave him speech in the cradle in the state of infancy to reject those Christians, so he said, "Surely I am the servant of God" [19:30]. Since it was in God's knowledge that Jesus would be the brightness of Mary's eyes and the joy of her heart in this world and the afterworld, the Lord of the Worlds placed the burden and pain of Jesus on her at the time of birth. He brought them a Book from Allah; if mankind and the Jinn tried to imitate ten chapters, or even one chapter of it, they will utterly fail in this task, even if they tried to do it by collective cooperation.

49.text:
The verse turns the announcement into a commission and puts the signs in the mouth of the one who would work them, and the whole passage is spoken as the messenger's own address to his people. "and make him a messenger to the Children of Israel to proclaim" states the office and names the people, and the sources read the office as the reason for the signs that follow, since the message carried to a people who asked for proof was given proof. "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord" opens the address and places the sign at its head, and the sources keep the sign as the argument for the truthfulness of the one who brought it. "I will make for you a bird from clay" gives the first of the signs, and the sources spell out the fashioning, the likeness shaped from the earth and then the breath blown into it. "breathe into it" marks the act that gives the shape its life, and the sources keep the two, the making and the breathing, as one work done by the leave of God. "and it will become a real bird—by Allah's Will" states the result and names the power behind it, and the sources read the last words as the fence that keeps the wonder from being taken as a claim of divinity. "I will heal the blind and the leper and raise the dead to life—by Allah's Will" gathers the healings and the raising, and the sources read the two illnesses as the cases in which a person is wholly helpless, so that the sign would stand plain, and they keep the raising of the dead beside them as the greatest of the three. "And I will prophesize what you eat and store in your houses" gives the knowledge of what is hidden, and the sources read it as the sign that reaches into the private life of the hearers. "Surely in this is a sign for you if you truly believe" closes the address with the condition, and the sources read the clause as the call to the hearer whose will is not yet bent, since the proofs are plain but the profit belongs to the one who accepts them. The verse before named the teaching given to him, and this one gives the commission that carried it to the people.

**The messenger sent to the Children of Israel.**

And He will make him to be a messenger to the Children of Israel during his tender years or after puberty. And He will teach him the Book and Al-Hikmah, and the Tawrah and the Injil And will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel (saying): (And will make him a messenger) after the age of thirty (unto the Children of Israel), and when he went to them he said: Scriptures, Wisdom and specially the Torah and the Injil; and that he will be sent as a Messenger of Allah to all of the Children of Isra il.

**The sign and the bird shaped from clay.**

"I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, that I design for you out of clay, a figure like that of a bird, and breathe into it, and it becomes a bird by Allah's leave; and I heal the blind, and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's leave. (Lo! I fashion for you out of clay the likeness of a bird, and I breathe into it) like the breathing of a sleeping person (and it is a bird) flying in the air, (by Allah's leave) by Allah's command. To be a messenger to the children of Israel I have come to you with a sign from your Lord I will create for you out of clay [something] like the shape of a bird then I will breathe into it and it will be a bird by the leave of God. Thus when God sent him to the Children of Israel he said to them ‘I am God’s Messenger to you’ and ‘I have come to you with a sign an indication of my truthfulness from your Lord and it is that I will create a variant reading for the particle introducing the relative clause annī ‘that I’ has innī ‘truly I’ indicating a new independent sentence that I will fashion for you out of clay like the shape of a bird ka-hay’at ‘something like the shape of’ the kāf is the subject of a passive participle then I will breathe into it fīhi the suffixed pronoun -hi refers to the preceding kāf and it will be a bird tayran is also read tā’iran by the leave the will of God. Then he fashioned for them a bat and when it became alive, they said: this is sorcery; do you have another sign? So he created for them a bat being the most perfectly-created of birds and they would watch it flying but when it went out of sight it would fall dead — so that the work of a creature sc.

**The blind, the leper and the dead.**

I will also heal the blind akmah is one that is blind from birth and the leper; these two are singled out for mention because with both afflictions the person is completely helpless. He Jesus was sent in an age of characterised by medicinal science and he cured through supplication fifty thousand in one day on the condition that each person would become a believer; and I bring to life the dead by the leave of God — He repeats this to preclude any false attributions of divinity to him — he brought back to life his friend ‘Āzar the son of an old woman and the daughter of the tithe-collector all of whom lived on and produced offspring and he also brought back to life Shem son of Noah but he died again immediately. I will cure the one who was born blind, so that he will be able to see, and the leper who will recover from his illness; and I will bring the dead to life. He said: yes, (I heal him who was born blind, and the leper) also, (and I raise the dead, by Allah's leave) by Allah's greatest Name: And when he did this, they said: this is sorcery, do you have any other sign?

**What the people ate and stored in their houses.**

(And I inform you of what you eat, and what you store in your houses) means, I tell you about what one of you has just eaten and what he is keeping in his house for tomorrow. I will tell you about what you consume and what you hide in your homes. He said: yes, (And I announce unto you what you eat) in the morning and at night (and what you store up in your houses) what you save from your lunch to dinner and from your dinner to the next day's lunch. I will inform you too of what things you eat and what you treasure up store in your houses and what I have never seen and he would inform people what they had eaten and what they would eat.

**The sign for the ones who believe.**

‘Surely in this there is a sign for you, if you are believers’ means that the proof, as presented, although complete in itself, would make sense only to one who wanted to believe; who had the ability to come out of his self and ponder over its veracity; whose nature was so receptive that the question of personal prestige did not become an obstacle to the acceptance of truth. In all of these extraordinary things that I mentioned to you, which human beings cannot do, is a clear sign that I am Allah’s messenger to you, if you wish to have faith and to accept the proof. Surely in that is a sign for you if you are believers. I have brought to you a sign indicating my prophethood: When he spoke for the first time in the temple, ‘all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers. It was on account of his miraculous personality and his astonishing powers of speech that, although he was born without a father, no one dared to abuse him on this score. However, the Jews had become so insensitive and insolent that, in spite of very clear proofs, they refused to believe in him. The message he will carry to them will be his argument in favour of his prophethood. Verse 50 says that Sayyidna Isa will declare that he has come to confirm Torah which was revealed before his coming and to make lawful what remained unlawful for them in the law of Moses.

50.text:
The verse continues the address of the messenger and gives the ground on which his teaching stands, and it ends with the call to fear God and to follow him. "And I will confirm the Torah revealed before me and legalize some of what had been forbidden to you" states the relation between the two books, and the sources read the confirming as the witness that the earlier book was true and the making lawful as the easing of some of what the earlier code had laid down, so that the messenger is placed in the line of the prophets and not against it. "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord" repeats the proof after the claim, and the sources read the repetition as the emphasis that the mission rested on the token given from on high and not on any human claim. "so be mindful of Allah and obey me" closes with the two duties, and the sources keep the fear of God first and the obedience to the messenger second, since the messenger commands only what God has commanded. The sources also record what was made lawful, the things that the earlier law had held back, and they read the easing as a mercy laid on the people who had carried the burden of the older code. The verse before gave the signs worked in the cradle and in the manhood, and this one gives the teaching that those signs confirmed, so that the easing of the law stands on the proof that the messenger brought with him.

**Confirming the Torah that came before him.**

Likewise I have come to you confirming that which was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you in it. Verse 50 says that Sayyidna Isa will declare that he has come to confirm Torah which was revealed before his coming and to make lawful what remained unlawful for them in the law of Moses. Likewise confirming that which was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you. I have come to you to confirm the revelation of the Torah that was before me, and to make lawful some of that which was unlawful in the past: making things easy for you. (And (I come) confirming) and I have come confirming Allah's divine Oneness in the Religion (that which was before me of the Torah) and all other Scriptures, (and to make lawful) to give you legal dispensation regarding (some of that which was forbidden unto you) such as the meat of camels, the fat of bovines and sheep, the Sabbath, and other things. (If you believe. And I have come confirming that which was before me of the Tawrah,) affirming the Tawrah and upholding it,. And He will teach him the Book and Al-Hikmah, and the Tawrah and the Injil And will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel (saying):

**The things that were made lawful for them.**

Thus he made lawful for them fish and birds which had no spikes; it is also said that he made it all lawful for them so that ba‘d ‘some’ means kull ‘all’. This means that the unlawfulness of some things in the earlier code would stand abrogated by the new one, (that of Sayyidna Isa) whose station of prophethood was the conclusive argument for that claim of abrogation. Scriptures, Wisdom and specially the Torah and the Injil; and that he will be sent as a Messenger of Allah to all of the Children of Isra il. (And will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel) means, that Allah will send 'Isa as a Messenger to the Children of Israel, proclaiming to them,. This part of the Ayah indicates that 'Isa abrogated some of the Laws of the Tawrah and informed the Jews of the truth regarding some issues that they used to dispute about. The Tawrah is the Book that Allah sent down to Musa, son of 'Imran, while the Injil is what Allah sent down to 'Isa, son of Maryam, peace be upon them, and 'Isa memorized both Books.

**The sign and the call to obey.**

I have come to you with a sign from your Lord He has repeated it for emphasis and to expand upon it so fear God and obey me in what I command you of affirming God’s Oneness and being obedient to Him. (I come unto you with a sign) with a token (from your Lord, so keep your duty to Allah) so fear Allah in that which He has commanded you with and repent to Him (and obey me) and follow my command and Religion;. I have brought to you a clear proof of the truthfulness of what I say, so be mindful of Allah by fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions; and follow that which I call you to. Once his prophethood is established, verse 51 states that Sayyidna Isa will ask them to beware of any contravention of Divine commandments, fear Allah, and follow his teachings in matters of religion which, in a nutshell, are that 'Allah is my Lord and your Lord' (the ultimate in belief) and 'Worship Him' (the ultimate in deeds).

**The ones who believed and the ones who refused.**

And when Jesus sensed their disbelief he said Who will be my helpers [in the cause of] Godḍ The disciples said We will be helpers of God; we believe in God; witness that we have submitted. When the message reached them and they differed-some of them believed him and some of them called him a liar and they were the majority-he came to know that prophecy does not spare one from affliction and the oppression of enemies. He said to his people Who will be my helpers [in the cause of] God so that they may help me in my exclusive devotion to His true reality and sincere dedication to His goalḍ Then those who were touched by the effects of [God's] providence āthār al-ʿināya and chosen through the effects of [divine] selection āthār al-takhṣīṣ said We will be helpers of God; we believe in God; bear witness to us in truth and let nothing come from us that would cast doubt on you. Jesus Christ was not only given extraordinary signs from God, but he spoke in so effective, persuasive and logical a manner that no one in his time could equal him. However, the Jews had become so insensitive and insolent that, in spite of very clear proofs, they refused to believe in him. ‘Surely in this there is a sign for you, if you are believers’ means that the proof, as presented, although complete in itself, would make sense only to one who wanted to believe; who had the ability to come out of his self and ponder over its veracity; whose nature was so receptive that the question of personal prestige did not become an obstacle to the acceptance of truth. The message he will carry to them will be his argument in favour of his prophethood. This, then, is the straight path which helps perfect the ideal combination of beliefs and deeds, leads to the way of salvation and is the source of communion with Allah. It was on account of his miraculous personality and his astonishing powers of speech that, although he was born without a father, no one dared to abuse him on this score.

51.text:
The verse closes the address with the plain word about the oneness of God, and it makes the worship of Him the whole of the path. "Surely Allah is my Lord and your Lord" puts the messenger and his people on one footing before the one Lord, and the sources read the sentence as the declaration of the oneness that both sides share, so that no one among them should take a partner beside God. "So worship Him alone" draws the duty out of the declaration, and the sources read the worship as the whole of the obedience owed to the Lord who has no partner. "This is the Straight Path" names the way that the address has set out, and the sources read the path as the religion that God is pleased with, the one that has no crookedness in it. The sources keep the three parts in the order given, the Lord first, then the worship, then the path, since the way is known from the one who owns it. The verse before gave the sign and the call to obey the messenger, and this one gives the plain word of oneness on which the whole call rests.

**The Lord of the messenger, and the people he was sent to.**

64.text:
The verse opens with the command that puts the call in the mouth of the Prophet, "Say, O Prophet", and what follows is addressed to "O People of the Book", the name given to the Jews and the Christians together, so that the invitation starts from what the two sides hold in common rather than from a quarrel. The invitation itself is "Let us come to common terms", and the sources read that word as a fair statement on which neither party loses anything and both can stand. What the common word carries is then spelled out in three clauses. "that we will worship none but Allah" is the first, and it is the ground on which the whole call is made, the Oneness that the earlier scriptures themselves carry. "associate none with Him" follows it, and it removes every partner, whether an idol, a saint or a created thing, from the worship that belongs to God alone. The third clause, "nor take one another as lords instead of Allah", turns from the idols to the people, because the sources explain the lordship named here as the obedience given to a person in what God has forbidden, which is how the learned of the two communities were followed by their people. The verse then turns to the answer that may come back. "But if they turn away, then say" prepares the messenger for a refusal and does not leave him without words, and the last phrase, "Bear witness that we have submitted to Allah alone", is the reply given, an announcement of what the Muslims hold and an end to the exchange. The sources draw a lesson of method from the shape of the verse: an invitation to what is agreed, spoken plainly, and a statement of one's own belief when the invitation is refused. The three clauses of the common word are therefore not a private demand of the Muslims but the content of what the earlier books taught, and the sources bring out that the whole exchange ends not with a verdict on the other side but with the Muslims stating what they are. The verse sets out the manners of an invitation, and it stands at the head of a group of verses that answer the claims of the People of the Book one by one.

**The principle the call is built on.**

This verse: unfolds an important principle of Tabligh (Preaching) and Da'wah (Preaching Islam). The principle requires that a person, who desires to carry his call to a group which holds beliefs and ideas different from his own, should follow a particular method. That method is to induce that group to unite only on what they both can agree to, for instance, when the Holy Prophet gave the Byzantine ruler, Hiraql (Heraclius) the call to Islam, he picked up a particular point on which there was mutual agreement, i.e., on the Oneness of Allah Almighty. This Ayah includes the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, and those who follow their ways. The call is made to a group with beliefs and ideas of its own.

**What the common word means.**

Jews and Christians come now to a word agreed upon sawā’ is the verbal noun meaning mustawin amruhā ‘a word regarding which the matter is upright’ between us and you and it is that we worship none but God allā is made up of an-lā ‘that…not’ and that we do not associate anything with Him and do not take each other for lords beside God’ as you have taken rabbis and monks; and if they turn their backs in rejection of God’s Oneness say you to them ‘Bear witness that we have submitted’ that we are of those who affirm the Oneness of God. (Say: O People of the Scripture. Come to an agreement) the agreement is: there is no god except Allah (between us and you: that we shall worship none but Allah) we shall declare Allah as the only One God, (and that we shall ascribe no partners unto Him) from among created beings, (and that none of us shall take others for lords beside Allah) that none of us shall obey another person in that which involves a transgression against Allah. O Jews and Christians, People of the Scripture, come let us unite on a fair word in which we are all equal: that we worship Allah alone and we do not worship anyone besides Him, no matter what his rank and no matter how high is his status; and that we do not take one another as lords to be worshipped and followed besides Allah. Come to a word that is just between us and you, that we worship none but Allah the same, and that we associate no partners with Him, and that none of us shall take others as lords besides Allah. (that is the same between us and you), an honest and righteous word that is fair to both parties. The concept of monotheism is not only a basic teaching of the Prophet Muhammad but is also enshrined as an established reality, even in the interpolated versions of the Torah and the Bible. Judged on this established criterion, Islam, unlike Judaism and Christianity, is proved to be a perfectly true religion. This concept of monotheism is preserved in its pure form only in Islam in the Quran. Other religions, while accepting monotheism ideologically, also adopted almost everything that ran counter to it.

**Worship none but Allah, and no lords besides Him.**

(that we worship none but Allah (Alone), and that we associate no partners with Him,) we worship neither a statue, cross, idol, Taghut (false gods), fire or anything else. Rather, we worship Allah Alone without partners, and this is the message of all of Allah's Messengers. ("and that none of us shall take others as lords besides Allah.") (And We did not send any Messenger before you but We revealed to him (saying): "None has the right to be worshipped but I (Allah)], so worship Me (Alone and none else).") [21:25] and,. No man should be accorded that special place which is the sole prerogative of the Lord of the Universe. While believing in God as the Sustainer, in practice they accorded that status to their saints. " In terms of realization, this is addressed to the folk of tawḤīd and the desirers on the road of the Haqiqah. He is saying, "If you who are traveling on the path of truthfulness today want to be dwellers in the seat of truthfulness [54:55] tomorrow, be careful to protect your walkway from the debris of customs, to sweep away the opacities of mortal nature from the carpet of your present moment, and to make the drinking place of your aspiration pure of the dust of others. Be one in heart, one in desire, and one in aspiration. 'When someone comes to have one concern, God will suffice him against the concerns of this world and the next.'" This is why He says, "and that some of us do not take others of us as lords apart from God": Do not obey the commanding soul, do not worship blameworthy caprice, and take not two gods; surely He is but One God [16:51]. As long as the talk of some defiled fellow grabs you, you're the servant of your own fancy, not a servant of God.

**The letter to Heraclius.**

I begin with the name of Allah who is All-Merciful, Very-Merciful. From Muhammad, servant of Allah, and His messenger: After that, I invite you to the call of Islam. Allah will bestow upon you a twofold reward, but should you turn away, then, on you shall be the sin of your subjects. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, Leader of the Romans: peace be upon those who follow the true guidance. Embrace Islam and you will acquire safety, embrace Islam and Allah will grant you a double reward. However, if you turn away from it, then you will carry the burden of the peasants, and,. So, how can this Ayah [3:64] be contained in the Prophet's letter to Heraclius before the victory of Makkah, and how can we harmonize between the statements of Muhammad bin Ishaq and Az-Zuhri? Therefore, it is possible that the Prophet wrote this statement (Say, "O People of the Scripture...") in his letter to Heraclius before the Ayah was revealed.

**The delegation of Najran and the Jizyah.**

Muhammad bin Ishaq and other scholars said that the beginning of Surah Āl-'Imrān, and more than eighty verses thereafter; were revealed about the delegation of Najran. Az-Zuhri stated that the people of Najran were the first people to pay the Jizyah (tax money paid to the Muslim State). However, there is no disagreement that the Ayah that ordained the Jizyah [9:29] was revealed after the Fath (conquering Makkah, and therefore, after the delegation of Najran came to Al-Madīnah). The answer is that the delegation of Najran came before Al-Hudaybiyyah (before the victory of Makkah), and what they paid was in lieu of the Mubahalah; not as Jizyah. The Ayah about the Jizyah was later revealed, and its ruling supported what occurred with the Najran people. In support of this opinion, we should mention that in another instance, the ruling on dividing the booty into one - fifth (for the Prophet) and four-fifths (for the fighters) agreed with the practice of 'Abdullah bin Jahsh during the raid that he led before Badr. An Ayah later on upheld the way 'Abdullah divided the booty. Later on, the Qur'an agreed with the Prophet's statement, word by word. It is also a fact that the Qur'an was revealed in agreement with what 'Umar said regarding the captured disbelievers at Badr, the Hijab (Muslim woman code of dress), refraining from performing prayer for the hypocrites, and regarding his statements: (And take you the Maqam (place) of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.)[2:125], and,.

65.text:
The address is again to "O People of the Book", and the question that follows is put to both communities at once: "Why do you argue about Abraham", who lived long before either of their religions existed. The argument is not over a small point, because the sources show that each group claimed him as one of its own, the Jews saying he was Jewish and the Christians saying he was Christian, and each supposed that following him settled the matter. The next phrase answers them from the order of time: "while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until long after him", so the religions in whose name the argument is made came into being long after the man they are claimed for. What they are doing is deciding a question about Abraham out of books that do not mention the answer. The verse closes with a question rather than a verdict, "Do you not understand", and the sources take those closing words as pointing at the failure of sense in what the two later communities claim about a man of the earlier time. The verse is the first of a series of corrections, since the verses that follow show that the same people argue about what they know little of and then about what they do not know at all. The correction is measured, because the point is not that they hold no scripture, but that the man they claim lived long before the scripture they hold.

The verse states the answer flatly, and it begins with a denial of both claims at once: "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian". Because the religions named after those two were founded long after him, the sources treat the sentence as a correction of a claim that could only be made by ignoring the order of time. What Abraham was is given in the second half, "he submitted in all uprightness and was not a polytheist", and every part of that carries weight. The submission is described by the word for turning away from every religion of the time towards the one worship of God, and the sources explain the word at length, because it is the same word by which the religion of Abraham is named afterwards: a straightness that keeps to the truth and does not swerve. The uprightness named in the phrase is therefore not a mood but a direction the whole life takes. The verse ends with the paired denial, "and was not a polytheist", and the sources keep the two clauses together, since the claim to follow Abraham is made by people who associate others with God, and the sentence rules that out in advance. 68.text:
The verse names those who stand nearest to Abraham, and it begins with the assertion that settles the argument: "Indeed, those who have the best claim to Abraham are his followers, this Prophet". The first of those named is the company that followed Abraham in his own lifetime, the people who accepted his call while he lived. The Prophet himself is named next, and the sources set out his claim as following Abraham in what his religion came to hold. The third name is "and the believers", which the sources take to mean the community of Muhammad, those who accepted the last messenger and the prophets before him, so that the nearest to Abraham are those who hold what he held rather than those who claim his name. The sentence ends by naming the one who keeps them: "And Allah is the Guardian of those who believe", a promise attached to the people named rather than to the claim, and the sources read it as protection and help given to all who believe in the messengers. The verse answers the claim made in the two verses before it, where each community claimed Abraham for itself, and it leaves the title with those who followed him. The word for the followers is the same one used of a household that stays with its head, and the sources apply it to those who kept to the way of Abraham while he was among them. On the Prophet it is applied because he came with what Abraham had been given, the worship of one God and the uprightness that goes with it. On the believers after him it is applied because they accepted what he brought and what the messengers before him brought, so that nearness to Abraham is measured by what a person carries and not by descent, and the last phrase names God as the one who keeps them in it. Alongside the naming of the three, the verse quietly answers the earlier claim, since the people who argued about Abraham are left out of the sentence and the title goes to the line of belief that runs through him.

69.text:
The verse names a wish rather than an act: "Some of the People of the Book wish to mislead you believers", and the sources read the wish as the settled intent of some of the learned among the Jews and the Christians to turn the Muslims from the faith they had been given, by argument where argument served them. The sentence then states where the attempt lands: "They mislead none but themselves", which the sources explain by the sin of the one who leads others astray resting on the leader while the guided are not moved by it, so that the harm returns to the hand that aimed it. The end of the verse gives the reason the harm is unseen by them, "yet they fail to perceive it", and the sources take that as a statement that they do not grasp the consequence of what they do, and do not see that their own loss is the loss the plan produces. The verse belongs to a run of warnings given to the same people, and the sources connect it with the two verses after it, which ask why they reject the signs of God and why they mix the truth with falsehood, so that the three together lay out the intention, the denial and the confusion of the books they claim. 70.text:
The verse opens with the address that has run through the passage, "O People of the Book", and it puts a second question to them: "Why do you reject the signs of Allah while you bear witness to their truth". The signs named are the verses of their own scriptures that carry the description of the messenger who was to come, and the sources read the question as aimed at the denial of what the books they hold already state. The two halves of the question are joined deliberately, since the denial is not the denial of a stranger but of a matter they themselves confirm, and the sources explain that the mention of their witness is there to make the charge heavier rather than to make the denial permissible in any condition. 72.text:
The verse records the plan itself, and it begins by naming the planners as a group: "A group among the People of the Book said to one another", which the sources identify as some of the leaders and the rabbis, gathered in a scheme to bring the believers back from what they had accepted. What they agreed on is then quoted: "Believe in what has been revealed to the believers in the morning and reject it in the evening", a show of faith at the start of the day and a public reversal at the end of it, and the sources report that the two ends of the day were taken from the dawn prayer and the later prayer, so that the reversal would be seen by the Muslims and spoken of by them. The intention behind the show is stated in the last phrase, "so they may abandon their faith", which the sources explain as the hope that the believers, seeing a learned people accept and then withdraw, would suppose that the learned had found something wrong in the religion and would follow them out of it. The verse is therefore not about a private opinion but about a method, and the sources notice that the beginning and the end of it were calculated together, since the reversal was meant to be public. The Muslims were warned of the scheme in advance, and the sources read that warning as part of the answer to it, because a plan that is known before it is carried out has lost the ground it stood on. The same group is told in the next verse that guidance is the gift of God, and the sources join the two verses here, since the answer to a plot against the faith is the statement that the faith is not in the hands of the plotters. The plan is quoted so that it may be answered, and the answer is that guidance and bounty are God's to give, which the verse after it states in full. The Muslims were not left to discover the scheme for themselves, and the sources read that as the mercy that guards a community from a plot it cannot see.

A community into which prophets and reformers have been born and in which religion has held sway for a considerable period of time, is often mistaken in thinking that their ethos and the truth are synonymous (that is, whatever they believe and practise is nothing but the truth). The verse continues the speech of the group and then breaks it with the words of God. The first part of their sentence is quoted in the plural, "And only believe those who follow your religion, Say, O Prophet, Surely", and the instruction it carries closes belief to their own community, since it tells the hearers to follow only those who follow them. The reply is put in the mouth of the messenger: "the only true guidance is Allah, s guidance", which the sources read as the answer to the claim that guidance belongs to a community, because guidance is the gift of God and not the possession of any nation. The speech of the group is then taken up again with "They also said", and what they said is quoted: "Do not believe that someone will receive revealed knowledge similar to yours or argue against you before your Lord, Say, O Prophet, Indeed", a warning given by one of them to another against accepting anyone outside their religion, and the sources explain it as the fear that the gift given to the Muslims would be matched or that the argument would be lost on the day they meet their Lord. The answer is given with the same opening as before, and it names where the gifts come from: "all bounty is in the Hands of Allah", which the sources apply to the scripture, the guidance and the direction of prayer being gifts rather than inheritances, then "He grants it to whoever He wills", so that no community has a claim on them, and last "And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing", generous in what He gives and knowing who is fit to receive it. The verse answers envy with the fact of ownership, and the sources read the whole passage as a correction of a religion that had been made into the property of a people. The two replies belong together, since the first denies that guidance belongs to a nation and the second denies that the gifts of God can be kept from anyone He chooses, and the passage leaves the reader with the plain statement that both come from the same hand. What the group feared was that others would be given what they had been given, and the verse answers that the giving was never theirs, so that the fear and the claim behind it fall together.
